docs.title: MediaCMS Documentation
docs.text:
MediaCMS is an open source video and media content management system. It runs on Django and React. It has a REST API.

MediaCMS stores video, audio, image, and PDF files. It encodes video into several resolutions. It can create subtitles with Whisper. It supports roles, categories, playlists, comments, and sharing.

Use this documentation to install MediaCMS, understand each role, and complete common tasks.

docs.title: Where to start
docs.text: Section Use it to Getting started Install, deploy, and sign in for the first time. Learn the main concepts. Roles See what each of the six roles can do. Compare the roles. Guides Follow step-by-step instructions for users, operators, administrators, and developers. Scenarios Follow one role through one path. Use scenarios as a script for a recording or a test. This version Check which MediaCMS version this documentation describes. What's new Read the changes in recent releases. Languages Find the languages that this documentation supports.

docs.title: MediaCMS Architecture
docs.text:
All pages in this documentation use the same system. A browser talks to the web server. The web server talks to Django. Django stores data in PostgreSQL. Celery workers encode video in the background.

flowchart LR
    browser["Browser"] --> nginx["nginx"]
    nginx --> uwsgi["uwsgi and Django"]
    uwsgi --> postgres[("PostgreSQL")]
    uwsgi --> redis[("Redis")]
    redis --> celeryWorker["Celery worker"]
    celeryWorker --> mediaFiles[("Media files")]
    uwsgi --> mediaFiles

docs.title: Writing guide
docs.text: Write MediaCMS documentation in clear, simple English. Follow the same spirit as ASD-STE100 for instructions. Do not copy the STE dictionary.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
1. Use one word for one thing. Check the glossary.
  2. Use the active voice. Prefer short sentences.
  3. Do not use idioms, slang, or filler such as "simply" or "please".
  4. Number the steps. Put one action in each step.
  5. Start each step with a verb: Open, Select, Enter, Set, Check, Clear.
  6. Put a condition in its own sentence before the action.
  7. Copy control labels from the screen and mark them in bold.
  8. Put notes and warnings in admonitions. They are not steps.
  9. Leave setting names, tokens, and placeholders unchanged.
  10. Keep UI labels in bold as the English words on the product screen when you translate a page.

docs.title: MediaCMS Architecture
docs.text:
Every role page and every task guide includes a heading MediaCMS Architecture.

  • Describe only the parts that persona uses on that page.
  • Put a Mermaid diagram under the heading when the task crosses more than one part of the system.
  • A single-screen action may use a short paragraph and omit the diagram.
  • Scenarios do not repeat this section. They link to the guide.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text: This section shows the path from a new server to a working MediaCMS portal.

docs.title: The path
docs.text:
1. Install with Docker. Download the code and start the containers.
  2. Deploy. Choose how people reach the portal: localhost, TLS, or a reverse proxy.
  3. First sign-in. Find the administrator password and sign in.
  4. Concepts. Learn the words that MediaCMS uses for media, states, and roles.
  5. Update. Keep MediaCMS current.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• You need a server with Docker and Docker Compose.
  • You need a user account that can run docker commands.
  • You need about 4 GB of free memory for a small portal.

Note

For a first test, use the default docker-compose.yaml file. You can change the deployment later.

docs.title: MediaCMS Architecture
docs.text:
The Docker image starts several services. The migrations service prepares the database and creates the first administrator. The web service answers browser requests. Celery services encode video.

    subgraph dockerHost["Docker host"]
        migrations["migrations container"]
        web["web container: nginx, uwsgi, Django"]
        celeryBeat["celery_beat container"]
        celeryWorker["celery_worker container"]
        db[("PostgreSQL")]
        redis[("Redis")]
    end
    migrations --> db
    web --> db
    web --> redis
    celeryBeat --> redis
    celeryWorker --> redis
    celeryWorker --> db

docs.title: Concepts
docs.text: Use this page to learn the words that MediaCMS uses. The glossary lists all terms.

docs.title: Media
docs.text: A media item is one uploaded video, audio, image, or PDF file. Each media item has a title, a description, a state, and an owner. Users can group media in playlists, categories, and tags.

docs.title: State: public, private, and unlisted
docs.text:
Every media item has one state.

State Who can find it Who can open it public Everyone, in listings, when the media is listable Everyone private The owner, editors, managers, and superusers The owner, editors, managers, superusers, and people with a direct share unlisted Nobody, in listings Anyone who has the URL

The setting PORTAL_WORKFLOW sets the state of new uploads. Its values are public, private, and unlisted.

docs.title: Encoding
docs.text:
MediaCMS encodes each video into the profiles that an administrator turned on. A long video is split into chunks. Celery workers encode the chunks and join them. MediaCMS then creates an HLS version.

The encoding status of a video is pending, running, fail, or success. Images, audio, and PDF files do not wait for video encoding.

docs.title: Listable
docs.text:
A media item is listable when all three conditions are true:

  1. The state is public.
  2. The encoding status is success.
  3. The media is reviewed.

Only listable media appears in public listings, such as the home page and search results.

docs.title: Review
docs.text: The setting MEDIA_IS_REVIEWED controls review. The default is True. All media counts as reviewed. If you set it to False, an editor, a manager, or a superuser must mark each new media item as reviewed. Until then, the media is not listable.

docs.title: Roles
docs.text: MediaCMS has six roles in addition to the pending state. See Roles for the full list and the role comparison.

docs.title: Manage pages and the admin portal
docs.text:
MediaCMS has two work surfaces. Do not mix them.

Surface Address Who uses it Manage pages /manage/media, /manage/users, /manage/comments Editors, managers, and superusers Admin portal /admin/ Staff and superusers
  • Manage pages are part of the portal. They list media, users, and comments with filters and bulk actions.
  • The admin portal is the Django administration interface. It shows a dashboard and the data tables.

A staff user can open the admin portal. A staff user cannot open the Manage pages unless the user is also an editor, a manager, or a superuser.

docs.title: Two upgrade words
docs.text:
• Content migration imports media from another platform, for example Kaltura, YouTube, or Panopto.
  • Site upgrade moves an existing MediaCMS install to a new MediaCMS version.

docs.title: MediaCMS Architecture
docs.text:
Django decides the listable value each time it saves a media item. Celery updates the encoding status. Reviewers set the reviewed flag.

flowchart LR
    upload["Upload"] --> stateCheck{"State is public?"}
    upload --> encodeCheck{"Encoding is success?"}
    upload --> reviewCheck{"Media is reviewed?"}
    stateCheck --> listableNode["Listable"]
    encodeCheck --> listableNode
    reviewCheck --> listableNode
    listableNode --> listings["Public listings"]

docs.text: Open Update or go to Roles.

docs.title: Deploy
docs.text:
Use this page to choose how people reach your MediaCMS portal.

The MediaCMS image uses supervisord. Supervisord runs one or more services in a container. You turn each service on or off with an environment variable set to yes or no:

  • ENABLE_UWSGI
  • ENABLE_NGINX
  • ENABLE_CELERY_BEAT
  • ENABLE_CELERY_SHORT
  • ENABLE_CELERY_LONG
  • ENABLE_MIGRATIONS

All services are on by default. To scale the portal, split the services into separate containers.

docs.title: Choose a pattern
docs.text:
Pattern Address Compose file Localhost http://localhost docker-compose.yaml Port 8000 http://localhost:8000 docker-compose.yaml with a port in FRONTEND_HOST TLS with Let's Encrypt https://my_domain.com docker-compose/docker-compose-letsencrypt.yaml Reverse proxy, HTTP http://mediacms.io docker-compose/docker-compose-http-proxy.yaml Reverse proxy, HTTPS https://mediacms.io docker-compose/docker-compose-https-proxy.yaml Scalable Your own address Your own orchestration

Note

After you change a setting, restart the services: docker compose restart web celery_worker celery_beat.

docs.title: Deploy on localhost
docs.text:
Use this pattern for tests. The main container runs migrations, the web service, celery_beat, and the Celery workers. It uses port 80.

  1. Open deploy/docker/local_settings.py.
  2. Set FRONTEND_HOST to http://localhost.
  3. Run docker compose up.

docs.title: Deploy with TLS and Let's Encrypt
docs.text:
Before you start, make sure the DNS record of my_domain.com points to your server.

  1. Open docker-compose/docker-compose-letsencrypt.yaml.
  2. Set VIRTUAL_HOST to my_domain.com.
  3. Set LETSENCRYPT_HOST to my_domain.com.
  4. Set LETSENCRYPT_EMAIL to your email address.
  5. Open deploy/docker/local_settings.py.
  6. Set FRONTEND_HOST to https://my_domain.com.
  7. Run docker compose -f docker-compose/docker-compose-letsencrypt.yaml up.
  8. Open https://my_domain.com. The browser shows a valid certificate.

docs.title: Deploy behind a reverse proxy
docs.text:
A reverse proxy receives browser requests and sends them to one or more web containers. The jwilder/nginx-proxy image can end TLS with self-signed, Let's Encrypt, or CA-signed certificates.

  1. Open deploy/docker/local_settings.py.
  2. Set FRONTEND_HOST to the public address, for example https://mediacms.io.
  3. Start the proxy Compose file that matches the address scheme.
  4. Check that DNS or your hosts file points the name to the proxy.

If you use your own proxy, send the media authorization requests to Django. See Use your own nginx configuration in Install with Docker.

docs.title: Scale the deployment
docs.text:
For a large portal, run these parts separately:

  • Many web containers.
  • One celery_beat container.
  • Many celery_worker containers.
  • A managed PostgreSQL database, a managed Redis service, and shared storage.

All web and worker containers must use the same media file system, for example NFS or EFS.

docs.title: MediaCMS Architecture
docs.text:
flowchart TB
    browser["Browser"] --> proxy["Reverse proxy and TLS"]
    proxy --> web1["web container 1"]
    proxy --> web2["web container 2"]
    web1 --> db[("PostgreSQL")]
    web2 --> db
    web1 --> redis[("Redis")]
    web2 --> redis
    redis --> worker1["celery_worker 1"]
    redis --> worker2["celery_worker 2"]
    worker1 --> storage[("Shared media storage")]
    worker2 --> storage
    web1 --> storage
    web2 --> storage

docs.text: Open First sign-in.

docs.title: First sign-in
docs.text:
Use this page to sign in to MediaCMS for the first time.

The user name of the first administrator is admin. The password depends on the Compose file.

Installation User name Password Development (docker-compose-dev.yaml) admin admin Production (docker-compose.yaml) admin Random, unless you set ADMIN_PASSWORD

Warning

Never use admin/admin on a portal that people can reach from the internet.

docs.title: Sign in on a development portal
docs.text:
1. Run docker compose -f docker-compose-dev.yaml up.
  2. Open http://localhost in a browser.
  3. Select Sign in.
  4. Enter admin in the user name field.
  5. Enter admin in the password field.
  6. Select Sign in.

The webpack development server also runs on http://localhost:8088. It shows the same pages with live frontend code.

docs.title: Sign in on a production portal
docs.text:
1. Read the migrations container output. Find the line Created admin user with password: ....
  2. Open your portal address in a browser.
  3. Select Sign in.
  4. Enter admin and the password from step 1.
  5. Select Sign in.
  6. Open your user menu. Select Change password. Enter a new password.

If you set ADMIN_PASSWORD in the Compose file, use that value in step 4.

docs.title: Check the result
docs.text: After you sign in, the header shows your user menu. The admin user is a superuser. It can open the Manage pages and the admin portal at /admin/.

docs.title: MediaCMS Architecture
docs.text:
The migrations container creates the admin user when the database has no such user. The script deploy/docker/prestart.sh reads ADMIN_USER, ADMIN_EMAIL, and ADMIN_PASSWORD. If no password is set, it makes a random one and prints it.

sequenceDiagram
    participant Operator
    participant Migrations as migrations container
    participant Database as PostgreSQL
    participant Portal as Web service
    Migrations->>Database: Run migrations
    Migrations->>Database: Create admin superuser
    Migrations-->>Operator: Print the admin password
    Operator->>Portal: Sign in as admin
    Portal->>Database: Check the password
    Portal-->>Operator: Show the signed-in portal

docs.text: Read Concepts.

docs.title: Install with Docker
docs.text: Use this page to install MediaCMS on one server with Docker Compose.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Install a recent version of Docker and Docker Compose.
  • Use PostgreSQL 15 or later. The development file docker-compose-dev.yaml and the default docker-compose.yaml use PostgreSQL 17.
  • Run the commands as a user that can use Docker.

Warning

MediaCMS version 3 and later needs PostgreSQL 15 or later. A data directory from PostgreSQL 13 does not start with a newer image. Migrate the database first. Read Update and Site upgrade.

docs.title: Install MediaCMS
docs.text:
1. Open a terminal on the server.

  2. Download the code.

    git clone https://github.com/mediacms-io/mediacms
cd mediacms

  3. Start the containers.

    docker compose up

  4. Wait until the output stops. Docker downloads the images and starts all containers.

  5. Open http://localhost in a browser. On a remote server, open http:// followed by the server IP address.

docs.title: Find the administrator password
docs.text:
The migrations container creates an admin user. It sets a random password unless you set ADMIN_PASSWORD in the Compose file.

  1. Read the end of the migrations container output.
  2. Find the line that starts with Created admin user with password:.
  3. Copy the password.
migrations_1     | Created admin user with password: gwg1clfkwf

To set your own password, remove the comment mark from ADMIN_PASSWORD in docker-compose.yaml before you run docker compose up.

See First sign-in to use the password.

docs.title: Fork beta and stable images (GHCR)
docs.text:
This fork publishes images to GitHub Container Registry. Change the Compose image: lines to test beta or stable builds.

Pull tag Meaning ghcr.io/mrjoshuap/mediacms:beta Latest successful beta base image ghcr.io/mrjoshuap/mediacms-full:beta Latest successful beta full image (Whisper) ghcr.io/mrjoshuap/mediacms:mediacms-next Same digest as :beta (branch alias) ghcr.io/mrjoshuap/mediacms:stable Latest stable base release ghcr.io/mrjoshuap/mediacms-full:stable Latest stable full release ghcr.io/mrjoshuap/mediacms:v1.2.3.YYYYMMDD Immutable pin for one release ghcr.io/mrjoshuap/mediacms:upgrade-audit-beta Base image alias for beta upgrade drills ghcr.io/mrjoshuap/mediacms:upgrade-audit Base image alias for stable upgrade drills

Example Compose override for beta:

services:
  web:
    image: ghcr.io/mrjoshuap/mediacms:beta
  celery_worker:
    image: ghcr.io/mrjoshuap/mediacms-full:beta
  migrations:
    image: ghcr.io/mrjoshuap/mediacms:beta

Beta builds publish a GitHub pre-release on every push to mediacms-next. Stable releases publish only when a stamp tag v1.2.3.YYYYMMDD (or v1.2.3.YYYYMMDD.N for a same-day emergency) is pushed from main. The product base version lives in version/FORK_VERSION.

Upstream Docker Hub images remain mediacms/mediacms and mediacms/mediacms:full.

docs.title: Enable Whisper transcription (optional)
docs.text:
Whisper creates subtitles automatically. It works only in the Docker installation. It needs a full image (mediacms/mediacms:full upstream, or ghcr.io/mrjoshuap/mediacms-full:beta / :stable on this fork).

  1. Use one of these methods.
    • Run docker compose -f docker-compose.yaml -f docker-compose.full.yaml up.
    • Edit docker-compose.yaml. Set the image of the celery_worker service to the full image tag you use.
  2. Open deploy/docker/local_settings.py.
  3. Set USE_WHISPER_TRANSCRIBE = True.

  4. Restart the services.

    docker compose restart web celery_worker celery_beat

docs.title: Use your own nginx configuration (optional)
docs.text:
MediaCMS uses nginx to protect media files. nginx asks Django if a user may open a file. If you use your own nginx configuration instead of deploy/docker/nginx_http_only.conf, copy these blocks from that file:

  • location = /_media_auth and location ~ ^/media/(encoded|hls)/(.*)$. They check access to encoded and HLS files.
  • location ~ ^/media/original/(.*)$. It checks access to original files. It sends unknown file types as downloads.
  • location ^~ /_protected_pdf/. Django uses it to serve PDF files. Without it, PDF files do not show.

docs.title: MediaCMS Architecture
docs.text:
docker compose up starts the services in this order. The database and Redis start first. The migrations container runs the database migrations and creates the administrator. The web and Celery containers start next.

flowchart TB
    dbService[("db: PostgreSQL 17")] --> migrations["migrations: migrate and create admin"]
    redisService[("redis")] --> migrations
    migrations --> web["web: nginx and uwsgi"]
    migrations --> celeryBeat["celery_beat"]
    migrations --> celeryWorker["celery_worker"]
    web --> mediaVolume[("media_files volume")]
    celeryWorker --> mediaVolume

Workers and web containers must use the same media file system.

docs.text: Choose a deployment pattern in Deploy. To update an installed portal, read Update.

docs.title: Update
docs.text:
Use this page to update a MediaCMS Docker installation to the latest image.

Warning

Back up the database and the media_files directory before you update. The default Docker layout stores PostgreSQL data in ../postgres_data/ and uploaded media in media_files/. Back up both locations, and verify a restore before you remove the old copy. A PostgreSQL major-version change may need a separate database migration; changing only the image tag can leave the data directory unusable.

docs.title: Update the image
docs.text:
1. Open a terminal on the server.

  2. Go to the MediaCMS installation directory.

    cd /path/to/mediacms/installation

  3. Download the latest image.

    docker pull mediacms/mediacms

  4. Stop the containers.

    docker compose down

  5. Start the containers.

    docker compose up

  6. Read the migrations container output. Check that the migrations finish without errors.

  7. Open the portal. Check that you can sign in.

docs.title: Check your custom nginx configuration
docs.text: If you use your own nginx configuration, compare it with deploy/docker/nginx_http_only.conf after each update. See Use your own nginx configuration in Install with Docker.

docs.title: Checklist before you change the image
docs.text:
Treat the database and the uploaded media as separate data sets.

  1. Stop the old services. Make a restorable PostgreSQL backup. Keep the original database version available until you test the backup.
  2. Back up the complete media_files/ directory, including encoded files, thumbnails, subtitles, and HLS output.
  3. Keep the old deploy/docker/local_settings.py, domain settings, and any reverse-proxy configuration.
  4. Test the update on copies of the database and the media directory first.

After you restore the copies into the Docker layout, start the database and Redis, run the migrations service, and only then start the web and Celery services. Check existing users, media, permissions, thumbnails, subtitles, and the encoding queue before you switch production traffic.

Do not load fixtures into an existing database. Do not delete the old PostgreSQL data or the media backup until the updated instance works.

docs.title: Update from version 2 to version 3
docs.text:
Version 3 uses Python 3.11 and PostgreSQL 15 or later. A data directory from PostgreSQL 13 does not start with a newer image. The PostgreSQL container shows this error:

FATAL:  database files are incompatible with server
DETAIL:  The data directory was initialized by PostgreSQL version 13, which is not compatible with this version 15.2.

Use one of these options:

  • Edit the Compose file. Use the postgres:13 image.
  • Migrate the database from PostgreSQL 13 to a newer version.

docs.title: Move to a new MediaCMS version with existing data
docs.text: A site upgrade moves an existing install to a new MediaCMS version. Only a superuser can run it. Read the Site upgrade guide.

docs.title: MediaCMS Architecture
docs.text:
An update replaces the application image. The database and the media files stay in volumes. The migrations container applies new database migrations on start.

flowchart LR
    newImage["New mediacms image"] --> migrations["migrations container"]
    migrations --> db[("PostgreSQL volume")]
    newImage --> web["web container"]
    newImage --> celeryWorker["celery_worker container"]
    web --> mediaFiles[("media_files volume")]
    celeryWorker --> mediaFiles

docs.text: Read the Site upgrade guide or go to Roles.

docs.title: Guides
docs.text:
Use these guides to do tasks in MediaCMS. Pick the guide set that matches your job.

Guide set Who reads it What it covers User Anyone who watches, uploads, or shares media Browse, search, upload, edit, captions, comments, playlists, share, trim, profile, download Operator Editors and managers Manage pages, review, categories, permissions, users Admin Staff and superusers The admin portal, processing, integrations, settings, site upgrade Developer People who change MediaCMS code Local development, architecture, tests, translations

docs.title: MediaCMS Architecture
docs.text:
All four guide sets use the same system. The guide sets differ in which part of the system they use.

flowchart LR
    U[User guides] --> P[Public pages and media pages]
    O[Operator guides] --> M[Manage pages]
    A[Admin guides] --> AP[Admin portal]
    D[Developer guides] --> C[Code and tests]
    P --> DB[(Database and media files)]
    M --> DB
    AP --> DB
    C --> DB
  • User guides use the public pages. These pages show media that is listable or that you can access.
  • Operator guides use the Manage pages: /manage/media, /manage/comments, and /manage/users.
  • Admin guides use the admin portal at /admin/.
  • Developer guides describe the code that runs all of the above.

Note

Do not mix the two surfaces. Editors and managers use Manage pages. Staff and superusers use the admin portal. See the glossary.

docs.title: Where to start
docs.text:
1. Read the User guides if you only watch or upload media.
  2. Read the Operator guides if you review media or manage people.
  3. Read the Admin guides if you configure the portal.
  4. Read the Developer guides if you change the code.

docs.title: Admin guides
docs.text:
Use these guides to run a MediaCMS portal from the admin portal at /admin/.

The guides are for staff and superusers. Use the glossary for the words in these pages.

Note

Editors and managers use Manage pages (/manage/media, /manage/users, /manage/comments). These guides cover the admin portal only.

docs.title: Who can do what
docs.text:
Task Staff Superuser Open the admin portal and the dashboard pages Yes Yes Change data in a list (only with the model permission) Yes Yes Read /api/v1/tasks Yes Yes Download a database backup No Yes Restore a database backup No Yes Use Migrations (/migrations) for content migration No Yes Run upgrade_site and other commands on the server Server access needed Server access needed

A staff user sees only the models that the account has permission to use. A group in the sidebar is hidden when it has no models for that account.

docs.title: Read in this order
docs.text: Step Guide Use it to 1 Admin portal map Find a page in the sidebar 2 Settings catalog Find the setting that controls a behavior 3 Moderation Handle reports, reviews, and comments 4 Library and engagement Manage media, categories, tags, playlists, and channels 5 Processing Manage encoding, captions, and FFmpeg settings 6 People Approve users and manage RBAC groups 7 Integrations Check identity providers, LTI, and migration records 8 Site health and database Check health, back up the database, read the task list 9 Custom pages and appearance Add pages, change the logo, add translations 10 Content migration Import media from Kaltura, YouTube, or Panopto 11 Site upgrade Move an existing install to a new MediaCMS version 12 Moodle and LTI Connect Moodle 13 SAML and identity providers Connect Microsoft Entra ID

docs.title: Two words for two jobs
docs.text:
• Content migration imports media from another platform (Kaltura, YouTube, Panopto). See Content migration.
  • Site upgrade moves an existing MediaCMS install to a new MediaCMS version. See Site upgrade.

Do not use one guide for the other job.

docs.title: MediaCMS Architecture
docs.text:
The admin portal is a Django admin with a workflow sidebar. Settings come from files. Data comes from PostgreSQL. Background work runs in Celery workers.

flowchart LR
    staff["Staff or superuser"] --> adminPortal["Admin portal /admin/"]
    adminPortal --> dashboards["Dashboard pages /admin/dashboard/section/"]
    adminPortal --> lists["Model lists and forms"]
    dashboards --> db[("PostgreSQL")]
    lists --> db
    settingsFiles["cms/settings.py and local_settings.py"] --> adminPortal
    lists --> celery["Celery workers"]
    celery --> redis[("Redis")]
    celery --> mediaFiles[("media_files")]
  • Settings files are not in the admin portal. A change to a setting needs a restart. See the Settings catalog.
  • Celery workers run encoding, captions, and trim jobs. See Processing.

docs.title: Content migration
docs.text:
Use this page to import media from another platform into MediaCMS. Supported sources are Kaltura, YouTube, and Panopto.

Warning

Content migration is not a site upgrade. Content migration imports media from another platform. A site upgrade moves an existing MediaCMS install to a new MediaCMS version. For a site upgrade, read Site upgrade.

Only a superuser can use content migration. The entry point is Migrations in the top right menu.

docs.title: Pages and URLs
docs.text:
Page URL List of migrations /migrations Choose a source /migrations/new New migration for one source /migrations/new/<source> where <source> is kaltura, youtube, or panopto One migration /migrations/<id> Edit a migration /migrations/<id>/edit REST API /api/v1/migrations

The source of a saved migration cannot change. To use another source, create a new migration.

docs.title: Compare the sources
docs.text: Kaltura YouTube Panopto Needs App token (service URL, partner ID, token ID, token value) yt-dlp. Cookies on servers API client and a local service account with admin rights What you give it Categories to migrate Video, playlist, or channel URLs Folders to migrate Owners Accounts are created or matched One MediaCMS user owns all media Accounts are created or matched Captions WebVTT, optional English only, if the uploader gave one If Panopto offers a caption file Reuse of existing encodings Yes, with Migrate media flavors / encodings Yes, with Attempt to skip transcoding No. One mp4 per recording. MediaCMS encodes RBAC groups Yes, with USE_RBAC No Yes, with USE_RBAC

docs.title: Run a migration
docs.text:
1. Open /migrations.
  2. Select New migration.
  3. Select the source.
  4. Enter the connection values for the source.
  5. Select Test connection. This reads counts and loads the choices. It imports nothing.
  6. Select the categories, folders, or URLs to migrate.
  7. Set the options.
  8. Select Save draft or Save and start. Nothing is imported until you start.
  9. Open /migrations/<id>. Watch the progress, the live log, and the ID mapping table.

Credentials are encrypted at rest. The API never returns a secret. Test connection makes the server contact the address in the form. For this reason only a superuser can use it.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
1. Back up the database and the media_files directory.
  2. Check the active encode profiles at /admin/files/encodeprofile/. They decide which encodings can be attached.
  3. Check the settings that change the result:
Setting Why it matters USE_RBAC Without it, private categories have no groups. Media still arrives private USE_LTI Needed to wire LMS courses to an LTI platform (Kaltura and Panopto) PORTAL_WORKFLOW and MEDIA_IS_REVIEWED See the listing rules in Library and engagement MIGRATION_PAGE_SIZE, MIGRATION_API_TIMEOUT, MIGRATION_DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT, MIGRATION_MAX_RETRIES Tune a large run

docs.title: Control a running migration
docs.text:
Button Result Pause Stops after the items in progress. Keeps the position Resume Continues from the saved position Abort Stops for good. Keeps what was imported. You can still restart it Run again Sweeps the source once more on a finished migration

Nothing is imported twice. MediaCMS stores a record for each imported object. A repeat run skips records that succeeded. It retries records that failed. It also picks up new items at the source.

Migration statuses: pending, running, paused, success, error, aborted. Record statuses: success, failed, skipped.

For Kaltura, Do not run between holds a run inside a window of hours. The time zone is the portal time zone. A page in progress is finished first.

docs.title: If a migration is stuck in running
docs.text:
1. Open the list. Read Last activity.
  2. If the time is old, a worker may have stopped.
  3. Select Pause.
  4. Select Resume.

Replaying a page is safe. Each importer checks the mapping table before it writes.

docs.title: Kaltura
docs.text:
• Create an app token with sessionType=2 (admin rights). A long expiry stops the token from ending a long run.
  • Enter Service URL, Partner ID, App token ID, and App token value. Do not add /api_v3 to the service URL.
  • Select at least one top-level category. Each top-level category is one site. Media that is only in other top-level categories is not migrated. Media in no category is migrated and arrives private.
  • Choose one user option: Migrate all users, Only migrate below listed users, or Only migrate users that own media.
  • Check the Global role mapping tab before you start. Super user and staff creates a Django superuser. A role is applied only to accounts that the migration creates.
  • Visibility comes from the categories of the entry. An entry in no category is private.

Kaltura groups can become RBAC groups with Migrate groups. A group gives no access until you attach it to a category.

docs.title: YouTube
docs.text:
• Install yt-dlp with pip install -r requirements.txt. Update it with pip install -U yt-dlp when extraction fails.
  • Enter one URL, playlist, channel, or video ID on each line.
  • Select the Owner. All media belongs to this one user.
  • From a server, YouTube can show a bot check. Paste a cookies file into Cookies file contents. Export it from a separate browser profile. Do not use that profile again.
  • YouTube never serves the original file. MediaCMS imports the best rendition that YouTube gives.

Note

Download only video that you own or that the licence allows.

docs.title: Panopto
docs.text:
• Create an API client of type User-Based Server Application.
  • Create a local Panopto service account with admin rights. SSO-only accounts do not work.
  • Select the folders to migrate. My Folder and Remote Recorders do not become categories.
  • Check downloads in the Test connection result first. If downloads are off, there is no file to import.
  • A public folder becomes a plain category. Other folders become RBAC categories when USE_RBAC is on.
  • Folders for LMS assignments become no category. Each submission stays with its student.

docs.title: After the run
docs.text:
1. Open /migrations/<id>. Check the counts for each object type.
  2. Open Integrations > Migration records. Filter by status failed.
  3. Search users for email-conflict.invalid. See People.
  4. Run Run again to retry failed items.
  5. Open Site > Health. Check the migration checks.

docs.title: MediaCMS Architecture
docs.text:
A migration is a Celery job. It reads from the source, writes records, and creates media, users, and categories.

flowchart LR
    superuser["Superuser at /migrations"] --> service["Migration service"]
    service --> provider{"Provider"}
    provider --> kaltura["Kaltura API"]
    provider --> youtube["yt-dlp for YouTube"]
    provider --> panopto["Panopto REST and SOAP"]
    service --> celery["Celery worker"]
    celery --> records[("Migration records")]
    celery --> media[("Media and files")]
    celery --> users[("Users and RBAC groups")]
    celery --> categories[("Categories and playlists")]
    media --> encoding["Encoding or reuse of source encodings"]
    adminPortal["Admin portal Integrations"] --> records

docs.title: Integrations
docs.text:
Use this page to check identity providers, SAML, LTI, and content migration records in the admin portal.

Open Integrations > Overview (/admin/dashboard/integrations/).

docs.title: Turn integrations on
docs.text:
Each integration has a switch in local_settings.py. A change needs a restart.

Setting Turns on Guide USE_IDENTITY_PROVIDERS Identity provider items, login options, user logs SAML and identity providers USE_SAML SAML configurations SAML and identity providers USE_RBAC Category groups. SAML and LTI use them People USE_LTI LTI 1.3 items Moodle and LTI

Migration services and records are always in the group. See Content migration.

Warning

USE_LTI = True sets SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE and CSRF_COOKIE_SAMESITE to None. It sets SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE and CSRF_COOKIE_SECURE to True. Use HTTPS. It also sets RELATED_MEDIA_STRATEGY to no_related.

docs.title: The Integrations overview
docs.text: Part What it shows Identity Providers Counts for ID providers and login options (when USE_IDENTITY_PROVIDERS is on) SAML Configurations Count of configurations (when USE_SAML is on) LTI Counts for platforms, tool keys, and launches (when USE_LTI is on) Migrations Counts of migrations by status: pending, running, paused, success, error, aborted Migration records Counts by status: success, failed, skipped Health checks Status of each integration check

docs.title: Health checks for integrations
docs.text:
Check Warns when Migration errors A migration is in the error status Migration record failures A migration record is failed Identity Providers USE_IDENTITY_PROVIDERS is on and no ID provider exists Active login options USE_IDENTITY_PROVIDERS is on and no login option is active SAML Configurations USE_SAML is on and no configuration exists LTI Platforms USE_LTI is on and no platform exists LTI Tool Keys USE_LTI is on and no tool key exists Failed LTI launches A launch log has success off

Select a check name to open the filtered list.

docs.title: Identity providers
docs.text:
When USE_IDENTITY_PROVIDERS = True, the group shows:

Item Use it to ID Providers Add an identity provider and its mappings User Accounts See accounts linked to an identity provider Login options Set the buttons on the sign-in page User Logs Read the SAML response logs

See SAML and identity providers.

docs.title: SAML configurations
docs.text: When USE_SAML = True, the SAML configurations item holds the SAML settings and group mappings for an ID provider. See SAML and identity providers.

docs.title: LTI
docs.text:
When USE_LTI = True, the group shows:

Item Use it to LTI platforms Add an LMS, for example Moodle LTI resource links See links between LMS resources and categories LTI user mappings See how LMS users map to MediaCMS users LTI role mappings Map LMS roles to MediaCMS roles LTI launch logs Read launches. Filter success off to find failures LTI tool keys Manage the keys that MediaCMS publishes

The LTI endpoints are under /lti/:

Endpoint Path Login start /lti/oidc/login/ Launch /lti/launch/ Public key set /lti/jwks/ Select media /lti/select-media/

See Moodle and LTI.

docs.title: Migration services and records
docs.text:
A superuser opens /migrations to start a content migration. The admin portal shows the stored data:

Item Use it to Migration services See each migration, its source, and its status Migration records Search, filter, and export the mapping of source IDs to MediaCMS IDs

Each imported object has one record. The status is success, failed, or skipped. A repeat run skips records that succeeded and retries records that failed.

Credentials are encrypted at rest with a key derived from SECRET_KEY. The API never returns a secret.

docs.title: MediaCMS Architecture
docs.text:
Integrations connect MediaCMS to other systems. The settings decide which parts exist.

flowchart LR
    idp["Identity provider: Entra ID or other"] -->|"SAML or OIDC"| allauth["django-allauth"]
    lms["LMS: Moodle"] -->|"LTI 1.3"| lti["LTI app /lti/"]
    source["Kaltura, YouTube, Panopto"] -->|"API or download"| migration["Migration service"]
    allauth --> users[("Users and RBAC groups")]
    lti --> users
    lti --> categories[("Categories")]
    migration --> media[("Media and records")]
    migration --> users
    migration --> categories
    adminPortal["Admin portal Integrations group"] --> allauth
    adminPortal --> lti
    adminPortal --> migration

docs.title: Library and engagement
docs.text: Use this page to manage media, categories, tags, playlists, and channels. Use the engagement page to see views, likes, dislikes, and comments.

docs.title: Open the library pages
docs.text: Page URL Library overview /admin/dashboard/library/ Engagement overview /admin/dashboard/engagement/ Media list /admin/files/media/

docs.title: The Library overview
docs.text:
Card or table What it shows Total media All media rows Media by state Public, Private, Unlisted Media by type Video, Audio, Image, PDF New media (7 days) Media added in the last 7 days Featured Media with the featured switch on Duplicate md5sum, Duplicate names Possible duplicates Categories, Tags, Playlists, Channels Totals. Each card opens a list Recent uploads One table for each type: video, audio, image, PDF

Note

Duplicate md5sum ignores media that has no md5sum value. Duplicate names and Duplicate md5sum are also health checks. See Site health and database.

docs.title: The Engagement overview
docs.text: The page shows total views, likes, dislikes, and comments. It also shows four top lists: most viewed, most liked, most disliked, and most commented media. Select a row to open the media.

docs.title: Media states
docs.text:
State Meaning public Can show in listings when it is listable private Shown only to the owner, editors, managers, shared users, and RBAC members unlisted Reachable by URL. Not shown in public listings

Media is listable when it is public, its encoding succeeded, and it is reviewed. PORTAL_WORKFLOW sets the state of new uploads. See the Settings catalog.

For image, audio, and PDF media, the public item shows at once. A video shows after one encoding succeeds.

docs.title: Work in the media list
docs.text:
1. Open Library > Media.
  2. Use the filters, the search box, or the date bar.
  3. Select the rows.
  4. Choose an action from the Action list.
  5. Select Go.

You can filter by state, review, encoding, reports, media type, downloads, comments, category, channel, and user. You can search by title, uploader username, or friendly token.

For the action names, see Moderation and Processing.

docs.title: Open related objects
docs.text: The media change page links to comments, encodings, actions, trim requests, caption requests, and playlists for that media. The Reports tab shows reported_times and the report actions.

docs.title: Categories and tags
docs.text:
1. Open Library > Categories or Tags.
  2. Select Add to create one. Select a row to edit it.

A category thumbnail is the first item that exists in this list:

  1. An image uploaded for the category.
  2. A tile from its most viewed media.
  3. static/images/category_default.jpg.

Replace static/images/category_default.jpg to change the default for the whole portal.

A portal manager can also edit a category title, description, and thumbnail on the category page. For an RBAC category, a manager of its group can do the same.

INCLUDE_LISTING_NUMBERS = False hides the media counts on /categories and /tags.

docs.title: Playlists and channels
docs.text:
• Open Library > Playlists to see playlists. The media in a playlist is edited in an inline table with order and media.
  • MAX_MEDIA_PER_PLAYLIST sets the limit for one playlist. The default is 70.
  • Open Library > Channels to see channels. A channel links to the media of its user.

docs.title: Upload limits
docs.text:
Setting Effect UPLOAD_MAX_SIZE Maximum size of one file in bytes UPLOAD_MAX_FILES_NUMBER Number of files in one upload NUMBER_OF_MEDIA_USER_CAN_UPLOAD Number of media one user may own. The default is 100 ALLOWED_MEDIA_UPLOAD_TYPES Allowed types. all turns the check off

MediaCMS removes a file that is not an allowed type.

docs.title: Share one media item
docs.text: Media permissions are direct shares on one media item: viewer, editor, or owner. Open Site > Media permissions to see them.

docs.title: MediaCMS Architecture
docs.text:
An upload creates a media row. Celery workers then create the files that the portal shows.

flowchart LR
    upload["Upload"] --> media[("Media row")]
    media --> original["Original file in media_files"]
    media --> celery["Celery workers"]
    celery --> derivatives["Thumbnails, sprites, preview, encodings, HLS"]
    media --> listable{"Public, encoded, reviewed?"}
    listable -->|"Yes"| listings["Public listings"]
    listable -->|"No"| hidden["Not in public listings"]
    category["Category and tags"] --> media
    playlist["Playlist"] --> media
    channel["Channel"] --> media
    engagement["Views, likes, comments"] --> media

docs.title: Moderation
docs.text:
Use this page to review media, handle reports, and manage comments in the admin portal.

Open Moderation > Overview (/admin/dashboard/moderation/).

docs.title: The Moderation overview
docs.text:
The page has two parts.

Part What it shows Media approval Media not reviewed, media approved in the last 7 days, recent media pending review, recently approved media Reports Reported media, media above the report limit, reports confirmed and cleared in the last 7 days, recent reports, recent report actions

Each card has an Open link. The link opens a filtered media list.

docs.title: Settings that change moderation
docs.text:
Setting Effect MEDIA_IS_REVIEWED False means new media must be reviewed before it shows in listings. The sidebar then shows Needs review. REPORTED_TIMES_THRESHOLD The number of reports that sets media to private. The default is 10. CAN_REPORT_MEDIA False hides the report button. ALLOW_ANONYMOUS_ACTIONS Includes report by default. An anonymous user can then report media. ADMINS_NOTIFICATIONS MEDIA_REPORTED and MEDIA_ADDED send email to ADMIN_EMAIL_LIST.

See the Settings catalog for all values.

docs.title: Review new media
docs.text:
Do these steps when MEDIA_IS_REVIEWED = False.

  1. Open Moderation > Needs review.
  2. Select the media rows to approve.
  3. Open the Action list.
  4. Select Mark as reviewed.
  5. Select Go.

Media is listable only when it is public, its encoding succeeded, and it is reviewed.

You can also change Is reviewed inline in the list. After the change, select Save.

docs.title: Handle a report
docs.text:
A user report adds a report action to the media and increases reported_times. At the threshold, MediaCMS sets the media to private.

  1. Open Moderation > Reported media.
  2. Open the media. Select the Reports tab.
  3. Read the reason in Extra info.
  4. Go back to the list. Select the media row.
  5. Choose one action from the Action list.
Action Result Confirm reports and set private Hides the media from public listings. Keeps the reports as evidence. Clear reports and keep private Deletes the reports. The media stays private. Clear reports and set public Deletes the reports. The media becomes public. Clear reports Deletes the reports. Does not change the state.
  1. Select Go.

Note

Private media can still be opened by the owner, editors, shared users, and RBAC members. Delete the media object to remove it fully.

Editors, managers, and superusers can clear reports from the admin portal.

docs.title: Reports above the limit
docs.text: Open Moderation > Above report limit to see media that reached REPORTED_TIMES_THRESHOLD. Use the same actions.

docs.title: Other media actions
docs.text:
The Action list in the media list has more actions. They need the change permission.

Group Actions Review Mark as reviewed, Mark as not reviewed State Set public, Set private, Set unlisted Switches Enable download, Disable download, Enable comments, Disable comments Feature Feature, Unfeature Owner Change owner (enter the new username) Files Delete original file

Encoding actions are in Processing.

These fields can be changed inline: Is reviewed, Featured, Allow download, Enable comments. Media state can be changed only with an action. This keeps the listable value correct.

docs.title: Delete the original file
docs.text:
This action removes the uploaded source file from disk. The media row and the encodings stay.

Before you start, check these conditions:

  • The media type is video or audio.
  • The original file exists on disk.
  • The encoding status is success.
  • At least one successful encoding exists that is not a preview.

  • No encoding that is not a preview is pending, running, or fail.

  • Select the media rows.

  • Select Delete original file in the Action list.
  • Select Go.
  • Read the page. It lists media that are allowed and media that are blocked.
  • Type I am sure.
  • Confirm.

Warning

New thumbnails, sprites, trim, re-encode, and captions need the original file. They fail until the file is uploaded again.

docs.title: Manage comments
docs.text:
1. Open Moderation > Comments.
  2. Search by text, uploader username, or media title.
  3. Select the comments to remove.
  4. Select Delete selected in the Action list.

Comments are also on the media change page as an inline table.

docs.title: Audit events
docs.text:
Moderator work writes MediaAction rows. Open Moderation > media actions to read them.

Action When it is written report_cleared Reports are cleared report_confirmed Reports are confirmed media_reviewed Media is marked as reviewed media_unreviewed Media is marked as not reviewed original_deleted The original file is deleted

The list is an audit log. You can view and delete rows. You cannot edit them.

docs.title: MediaCMS Architecture
docs.text:
A report starts on the public site. Staff then finish the work in the admin portal.

flowchart LR
    user["Viewer or anonymous user"] -->|"Report"| api["API /api/v1/media/token/actions"]
    api --> mediaAction[("MediaAction report rows")]
    api --> media[("Media reported_times")]
    media -->|"At REPORTED_TIMES_THRESHOLD"| privateState["State set to private"]
    media --> notify["Email to ADMIN_EMAIL_LIST"]
    staff["Staff or editor"] --> queues["Reported media and Above report limit"]
    queues --> actions["Confirm or clear actions"]
    actions --> media
    actions --> audit[("MediaAction audit rows")]

docs.title: Moodle and LTI
docs.text: Use this page to connect Moodle to MediaCMS with LTI 1.3 and the MediaCMS Moodle plugins. Lecturers and students then use My Media and embed media inside Moodle.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Use the same domain for Moodle and MediaCMS. For example, use moodle.organisation.org and mediacms.organisation.org. Browsers block cross-site content more and more. A shared parent domain avoids limits on embedded media.
  • Use HTTPS. With USE_LTI = True, MediaCMS sets secure cookies with SameSite=None.
  • You need admin access to Moodle and to MediaCMS.

docs.title: Step 1: Turn on the MediaCMS settings
docs.text:
1. Open local_settings.py (deploy/docker/local_settings.py for Docker Compose).
  2. Add these lines.
USE_IDENTITY_PROVIDERS = True
USE_RBAC = True
USE_LTI = True
  1. Restart the services.
docker compose restart web celery_worker celery_beat

The Integrations group now shows the LTI items. See Integrations.

docs.title: Step 2: Add MediaCMS as an external tool in Moodle
docs.text:
Open Moodle: Site Administration > Plugins > Activity Modules > External tools > Manage Tools > Configure a Tool Manually.

Replace https://mediacms.organisation.org with your MediaCMS URL.

Field Value Name MediaCMS Tool URL https://mediacms.organisation.org/lti/launch/ LTI version LTI 1.3 Client ID Moodle gives it after you save Public key type Keyset URL Public keyset https://mediacms.organisation.org/lti/jwks/ Initiate login URL https://mediacms.organisation.org/lti/oidc/login/ Redirection URI(s) https://mediacms.organisation.org/lti/launch/ Tool configuration usage Show in activity chooser and as a preconfigured tool Default launch container Embed, without blocks. Supports Deep Linking

Set the services:

Service Value IMS LTI Assignment and Grade Services Do not use this service IMS LTI Names and Role Provisioning Use this service to retrieve members' information as per privacy settings Tool Settings Use this service

Set the privacy:

Field Value Share launcher's name with tool Always Share launcher's email with tool Always Accept grades from the tool As specified in Deep Linking definition, or Delegate to teacher

Select Save changes.

docs.title: Step 3: Install the Moodle plugins
docs.text:
The integration uses two plugins:

Plugin Purpose filter_mediacms The filter. It has the shared settings (MediaCMS URL, LTI tool). It embeds media with LTI 1.3 tiny_mediacms The TinyMCE button that inserts media. It needs filter_mediacms

The ZIP files are in lms-plugins/mediacms-moodle/dist/ in the MediaCMS repository. Use the newest version in that folder.

  1. Open Moodle: Site Administration > Install plugins.
  2. Upload the filter_mediacms ZIP. Finish the install.
  3. Upload the tiny_mediacms ZIP. Finish the install.

Install filter_mediacms first. Moodle does not install tiny_mediacms without it.

You can also unzip filter_mediacms into the filter/ directory. Unzip tiny_mediacms into lib/editor/tiny/plugins/. Then open Moodle. This method can be automated.

docs.title: Step 4: Configure the plugins in Moodle
docs.text:
1. Open Plugins > Filters > Manage Filters.
  2. Set MediaCMS to Enable. Move it to the top of the list.
  3. Open Plugins > Filters > MediaCMS.
  4. Set My Media link placement to Top Navigation or User Navigation.
  5. Enter MediaCMS URL. For example, mediacms.organisation.org.
  6. Enter LTI Tool. For example, mediacms.organisation.org/lti/launch/.
  7. Set Share Embedded Media. See the next section.
  8. Open Plugins > Text editors > TinyMCE > MediaCMS.
  9. Set the default embed options: Show video title, Link video title, Show user avatar.

docs.title: Share Embedded Media
docs.text:
Value Result True A user who opened embedded media can find it in My Media > Shared with Me False A user cannot find embedded media in Shared with Me. Use this for strict access control

MediaCMS sets embedded media to Shared (private and shared). Users who open the Moodle activity become sharing partners. Their permission is not removed when Moodle access is removed. A lecturer or administrator removes these permissions with My Media > Bulk Actions > Course Cleanup.

docs.title: Step 5: Add Moodle as an LTI platform in MediaCMS
docs.text:
1. Open the admin portal. Open Integrations > LTI platforms.
  2. Select Add LTI platform.
  3. Enter the values.
Section Field Value Basic Information Name A name for your use Basic Information Platform ID The Moodle issuer URL. For example, https://moodle.organisation.org Basic Information Client ID From Moodle: External tools > Manage Tools > MediaCMS > Edit OIDC Endpoints Auth login URL https://moodle.organisation.org/filter/mediacms/lti_auth.php OIDC Endpoints Auth token URL https://moodle.organisation.org/mod/lti/token.php OIDC Endpoints Auth audience https://moodle.organisation.org/mod/lti/certs.php JWK Configuration Key set URL https://moodle.organisation.org/mod/lti/certs.php Deployment & Features Deployment IDs From Moodle: Manage Tools > MediaCMS > View configuration details Deployment & Features Enable NRPS On Deployment & Features Enable deep linking On Auto-Provisioning Settings Remove from groups on unenroll On
  1. Select Save.

docs.title: Step 6: Test
docs.text:
1. Sign in to Moodle as an administrator, a lecturer, and a student.
  2. Open My Media for each account.
  3. In MediaCMS, open Integrations > LTI launch logs. Check that launches show success.
  4. Open Site > Health. Check the LTI checks.

docs.title: How courses and roles map
docs.text:
A Moodle course is a category in MediaCMS. A course category is created when:

  • A lecturer shares media with course members.
  • A lecturer publishes media to a course.
  • A lecturer inserts MediaCMS media in a course element with the TinyMCE button.
Moodle role MediaCMS category role Student Viewer (member) Teacher Manager

MediaCMS adds a user to the course group when that user opens My Media or opens embedded media in Moodle. Roles are synchronized at the same time. There is no continuous synchronization with NRPS yet. A user who leaves a course is removed from the course group only when that user, or a course member, opens My Media in Moodle again. Set Remove from groups on unenroll for this.

docs.title: Course cleanup
docs.text:
A lecturer or administrator can use My Media > Bulk Actions > Course Cleanup:

  • Remove present course permissions for all course members removes users as sharing partners. It does not remove their access when they still have access in Moodle.
  • Remove Comments deletes comments on the embedded course media.

Students cannot use Course Cleanup.

docs.title: MediaCMS Architecture
docs.text:
Moodle starts an LTI launch. MediaCMS checks the platform, finds or creates the course category and group, and shows the media.

sequenceDiagram
    participant U as User in Moodle
    participant M as Moodle
    participant C as MediaCMS /lti/
    participant D as Database
    U->>M: Open My Media or an embedded media
    M->>C: Start login /lti/oidc/login/
    C->>M: Redirect to Moodle auth login URL
    M->>C: Launch /lti/launch/ with signed token
    C->>D: Find LTI platform, check keys
    C->>D: Find or create user, course category, RBAC group
    C->>M: Show media in the frame

docs.title: Custom pages and appearance
docs.text: Use this page to add custom pages, add links to the sidebar, add code to every page, change the logo, and add translations.

docs.title: Custom pages
docs.text: A custom page is a Page row. You edit it in the admin portal with a rich text editor.

docs.title: Create a page
docs.text:
1. Open the admin portal.
  2. Open Site > Pages.
  3. Select Add page.
  4. Enter the Title. The Slug is filled from the title.
  5. Check the Slug. See the rules below.
  6. Enter the content in the editor.
  7. Select Save.

After you save, the list shows the public address in Page URL. Select it to open the page.

Note

MediaCMS adds sandbox="allow-scripts allow-same-origin allow-presentation" to each iframe in the content.

docs.title: Slug rules
docs.text:
The slug decides the address and the place of the page.

Rule Detail Characters Lowercase letters and digits. Words are joined by one hyphen. For example, staff-handbook Not allowed Uppercase, underscores, double hyphens, a hyphen at the start or end Reserved names See the next list Result of a wrong slug The page is not saved. The form shows a message

Messages:

Message Cause That address is reserved. The slug or the page name is a reserved name The page name is not a valid address. The slug does not follow the character rules That sidebar link is already built in. A sidebar link uses a built-in name

docs.title: Protected slugs
docs.text:
These names are used by MediaCMS routes. You cannot use them as a slug, or as a page name after sidebar-<section>--.

accounts, login, logout, signup, password, saml, approval_required, api, api-auth, swagger, docs, admin, lti, tinymce, fu, manage, user, channel

A page that has a protected slug is not served as a public page. This matters for a site upgrade.

docs.title: Built-in pages
docs.text:
Slug Result about Replaces the default About page tos Replaces the placeholder terms of service page

The names about, tos, contact, and setlanguage are built in. You cannot use them as the name of a sidebar link.

docs.title: Public address
docs.text:
Slug Address staff-handbook /staff-handbook sidebar-info--staff-handbook /staff-handbook (and a link in the sidebar)

MediaCMS looks for an exact slug first. Then it looks for a sidebar page with that name.

docs.title: Add a link to the sidebar
docs.text:
Start the slug with sidebar-<section>--. Use two hyphens before the page name. The title of the page is the text of the link.

Section Slug starts with Who sees the link Browse sidebar-browse-- Everyone Library sidebar-library-- Signed-in users Personal sidebar-personal-- Signed-in users Info sidebar-info-- Everyone Manage sidebar-manage-- Editors, managers, and superusers

Example: the slug sidebar-info--staff-handbook makes a link in the info section of the sidebar. The link opens /staff-handbook.

Pages are listed in alphabetical order of the title.

docs.title: Add HTML to the sidebar
docs.text:
A page with one of these slugs is not a public page. MediaCMS puts its content in a slot.

Slug starts with Slot sidebar-below-- Below the navigation menu sidebar-after-theme-- Below the theme switcher sidebar-footer-- In the sidebar footer

Example: sidebar-footer--contact-block.

For plain text in the footer, set SIDEBAR_FOOTER_TEXT in local_settings.py.

docs.title: Add code to every page
docs.text:
A page with one of these slugs adds its content to every page. These pages are not public pages.

Slug Where the content goes inject-head In the head element inject-css In a style element inject-header In the page header inject-footer In the page footer inject-js In a script element at the end of the page

Warning

Content of these pages is not escaped. Anyone who can edit a page can run code on every page. Give the page permission only to people that you trust.

For CSS files, you can also set EXTRA_CSS_PATHS in local_settings.py. Put the file in static/css/. For example, EXTRA_CSS_PATHS = ["/static/css/custom.css"].

docs.title: Change the logo
docs.text:
The portal has one logo for the light theme and one for the dark theme. PORTAL_LOGO_DARK_* is the logo for the light theme. It is a dark logo on a light page. PORTAL_LOGO_LIGHT_* is the logo for the dark theme.

Setting Default PORTAL_LOGO_DARK_SVG /static/images/logo_dark.svg PORTAL_LOGO_DARK_PNG /static/images/logo_dark.png PORTAL_LOGO_LIGHT_SVG /static/images/logo_light.svg PORTAL_LOGO_LIGHT_PNG /static/images/logo_dark.png
  1. Put the new files in static/images/.
  2. Open local_settings.py.
  3. Set the paths. For example:
PORTAL_LOGO_DARK_SVG = "/static/images/my_logo_dark.svg"
PORTAL_LOGO_LIGHT_SVG = "/static/images/my_logo_light.svg"
  1. To use PNG files only, set the SVG settings to empty strings. Set the PNG settings.
  2. Restart the services.

An SVG file has priority over a PNG file when both are set.

Other appearance settings: PORTAL_NAME, PORTAL_DESCRIPTION, DEFAULT_THEME, USE_ROUNDED_CORNERS. See the Settings catalog.

docs.title: Translations
docs.text:
MediaCMS has two kinds of text:

Kind Where it lives Rebuild needed Django template text templates/ No React text frontend/ Yes. Run make build-frontend

Warning

This workflow is required. A change that skips it is not accepted.

docs.title: Add a translatable string
docs.text:
1. Mark the string as translatable in the code.
  2. Django templates: see how templates/cms/about.html does it.
  3. React: see how translateString is used in frontend/.
  4. Add the string to files/frontend_translations/en.py first.
  5. Run the command that copies the new string into all language files.
python manage.py process_translations

With the development stack:

docker compose -f docker-compose-dev.yaml exec -T web python manage.py process_translations
  1. Open the file of your language in files/frontend_translations/. For example, de.py.
  2. Translate the string.
  3. For React text, run the build.
make build-frontend

The command process_translations adds missing keys to every language file except en.py. The new key gets the English text until someone translates it. It also sorts the keys. You do not need to translate into all languages. You must run the command.

Do not change the key text of an existing string. Keep setting names, tokens, and placeholders unchanged.

docs.title: Improve an existing translation
docs.text:
1. Find the language code in files/frontend_translations/.
  2. Edit the matching file. For example, fr.py.
  3. For React text, run make build-frontend.

docs.title: Set the default language
docs.text:
1. Open local_settings.py.
  2. Set LANGUAGE_CODE to a code from LANGUAGES. For example, LANGUAGE_CODE = "de".
  3. Restart the services.

To remove a language from the list, remove it from LANGUAGES. To change the language for one browser, use the globe icon in the admin navbar, or /setlanguage on the public site. Both set the django_language cookie.

docs.title: Add a new language
docs.text:
1. Add the language to LANGUAGES in local_settings.py.
  2. Copy files/frontend_translations/en.py to a new file in the same folder.
  3. Translate the strings.
  4. Run python manage.py process_translations.
  5. Run make build-frontend.

Site > Languages lists caption languages. It is not the list of interface languages.

docs.title: MediaCMS Architecture
docs.text:
Pages and settings are read on each request and passed to the templates. Translations are files in the code.

flowchart LR
    editor["Staff in admin portal"] --> pageRow[("Page rows")]
    pageRow --> processor["Context processor"]
    settingsFile["local_settings.py: logo, name, theme"] --> processor
    processor --> sidebar["Sidebar groups and HTML slots"]
    processor --> inject["Head, CSS, header, footer, JS"]
    processor --> logo["Logo"]
    publicRoute["/slug route"] --> pageRow
    enPy["files/frontend_translations/en.py"] --> command["process_translations"]
    command --> langFiles["Language files de.py, fr.py, ..."]
    langFiles --> react["React bundle: make build-frontend"]
    langFiles --> templates["Django templates"]

docs.title: People
docs.text:
Use this page to manage user accounts, approval, roles, and RBAC groups in the admin portal.

Open People > Overview (/admin/dashboard/people/).

docs.title: The People overview
docs.text:
Part What it shows Totals Total users, approved users, users waiting for approval, inactive users Roles Superusers, staff users, managers, editors, regular users Activity New users (7 days), active users (30 days), recently registered users Top lists Top uploaders by count and by size, top commenters, top likers, top dislikers, top reporters Approval Recent users waiting for approval (when approval is on)

Select a user name to open the user.

docs.title: User roles
docs.text:
Set these fields on the user change page.

Field Result Is active Off blocks sign-in. The account is inactive Is staff Opens the admin portal Is superuser Full access to the portal and the admin portal MediaCMS Manager (is_manager) Can manage users in Manage pages. Not Django staff by itself MediaCMS Editor (is_editor) Can open Manage media and comments advanced user (advancedUser) Can add media or comment when CAN_ADD_MEDIA or CAN_COMMENT is advancedUser Is approved Shows only when USERS_NEEDS_TO_BE_APPROVED = True

You can filter the list by active, superuser, staff, editor, manager, regular user, recently joined, and active uploader.

docs.title: Actions for users
docs.text:
1. Open People > users.
  2. Select the user rows.
  3. Choose an action in the Action list.
  4. Select Go.
Action Result Approve users Sets Is approved Unapprove users Clears Is approved Deactivate users Sets Is active off Reactivate users Sets Is active on

docs.title: Approve new users
docs.text:
Do these steps when USERS_NEEDS_TO_BE_APPROVED = True.

  1. Open People > Waiting for approval.
  2. Select the user rows.
  3. Select Approve users in the Action list.
  4. Select Go.

You can also select Is approved in the list and then select Save.

A pending user can sign in. The pending user can browse. Upload, edit, and Manage pages are refused until approval.

docs.title: Control registration
docs.text:
Setting Effect USERS_CAN_SELF_REGISTER False closes sign-up. This is the server rule REGISTER_ALLOWED False hides the register button only LOGIN_ALLOWED False hides the sign-in button only. The sign-in page still works ALLOWED_DOMAINS_FOR_USER_REGISTRATION Only these email domains can register. An empty list turns the check off RESTRICTED_DOMAINS_FOR_USER_REGISTRATION These email domains cannot register ACCOUNT_EMAIL_VERIFICATION optional, mandatory, or none GLOBAL_LOGIN_REQUIRED True makes the whole portal available only to signed-in users

See the Settings catalog.

docs.title: Email addresses
docs.text: Open People > email addresses to see the email addresses that django-allauth stores. Use it to check if an address is verified.

docs.title: RBAC groups
docs.text:
RBAC adds category access for groups. It shows in the sidebar only when USE_RBAC = True.

  1. Create a group.
  2. Attach one or more categories to the group.
  3. Add users to the group with a role.
Role What it allows in the attached categories member See all media, also private media contributor All of member, and edit media and add media to the category manager All of contributor, and owner-level access to every media in the category

To create a group:

  1. Open People > RBAC groups.
  2. Select Add.
  3. Enter the name. Select the categories.
  4. Select Save.

To add a user:

  1. Open People > RBAC memberships.
  2. Select Add.
  3. Select the user, the group, and the role.
  4. Select Save.

An RBAC category is hidden from the public category list for people outside the group.

Note

A Kaltura or Panopto content migration can create RBAC groups. It adds members and never changes them on a later run. See Content migration.

docs.title: Find accounts that need a decision
docs.text: A content migration can create accounts with an email on the email-conflict.invalid domain. Search users for email-conflict.invalid. Set a real email or merge the accounts by hand.

docs.title: MediaCMS Architecture
docs.text:
A user has flags for portal roles. RBAC adds access through a group.

flowchart LR
    user["User"] --> flags["Flags: staff, superuser, manager, editor, advanced, approved"]
    user --> membership["RBAC membership with role"]
    membership --> group["RBAC group"]
    group --> category["Category"]
    category --> media["Media in the category"]
    flags --> adminPortal["Admin portal and Manage pages"]
    approvalSetting["USERS_NEEDS_TO_BE_APPROVED"] --> flags
    rbacSetting["USE_RBAC"] --> membership

docs.title: Admin portal map
docs.text: Use this page to find an item in the admin portal sidebar. The sidebar has six groups. Each group has an overview page at /admin/dashboard/<section>/.

docs.title: Sidebar groups
docs.text:
Group Overview page Guide Moderation /admin/dashboard/moderation/ Moderation Library /admin/dashboard/library/ and /admin/dashboard/engagement/ Library and engagement Processing /admin/dashboard/processing/ Processing People /admin/dashboard/people/ People Integrations /admin/dashboard/integrations/ Integrations Site /admin/dashboard/health/, configuration/, system/, and database/ Site health and database

The first item in each group opens the overview page. The Library group also has Engagement. The Site group has four pages: Health, Configuration, System, and Database.

docs.title: Items in each group
docs.text:
Some items show only when a setting is on or a model permission is present.

Group Items Condition Moderation Overview, Reported media, Above report limit, media actions, comments Media permissions needed for the queue links Moderation Needs review MEDIA_IS_REVIEWED = False Library Overview, Engagement, media, categories, tags, playlists, channels None Processing Overview, Encoding queue, Failed encodings, encodings, captions, caption requests, trim requests None People Overview, users, email addresses None People Waiting for approval USERS_NEEDS_TO_BE_APPROVED = True People RBAC groups, RBAC memberships USE_RBAC = True Integrations Overview, migration services, migration records None Integrations ID providers, user accounts, login options, user logs USE_IDENTITY_PROVIDERS = True Integrations SAML configurations USE_SAML = True Integrations LTI platforms, resource links, user mappings, role mappings, launch logs, tool keys USE_LTI = True Site Health, Configuration, System, Database None Site Pages, licenses, encode profiles, languages, media permissions, sites None

docs.text:
Page URL Use it to Dashboard /admin/ See totals and open an overview page Get Support /admin/dashboard/support/ Download a redacted support bundle Database backup /admin/dashboard/database/backup/ Download a backup (superuser) Database restore /admin/dashboard/database/restore/ Upload a backup on an initial install (superuser)

All dashboard URLs end with a slash. An unknown section gives a 404 page.

docs.title: Refresh the numbers
docs.text:
Dashboard numbers are cached for 60 seconds.

  1. Open any dashboard page.
  2. Select Refresh stats.

The page reloads with ?refresh_stats=1. Only a staff user can force a refresh.

docs.title: Change the language
docs.text:
1. Select the globe icon in the admin navbar.
  2. Select a language.

The choice is stored in the django_language cookie. It also applies to the public site.

docs.title: MediaCMS Architecture
docs.text:
The sidebar is built on each request from the models that the signed-in account may use. A setting can add or remove an item.

flowchart TD
    request["Admin request"] --> rawList["Django app list for this account"]
    rawList --> builder["Workflow sidebar builder"]
    settingsFile["Settings: MEDIA_IS_REVIEWED, USERS_NEEDS_TO_BE_APPROVED, USE_RBAC, USE_SAML, USE_LTI, USE_IDENTITY_PROVIDERS"] --> builder

    people --> overview
    integrations --> overview
