    overview --> cache[("Redis cache 60 seconds")]

Note

The real app indexes such as /admin/files/ still work for bookmarks.

docs.title: Processing
docs.text:
Use this page to manage encoding, encode profiles, FFmpeg settings, Whisper captions, and trim requests.

Open Processing > Overview (/admin/dashboard/processing/).

docs.title: The Processing overview
docs.text:
Part What it shows Encodings Encoding queue, and media counts by encoding status: Pending, Running, Success, Failed Caption Requests Counts by status: pending, running, success, fail Trim Requests Counts by status: initial, running, success, fail

Each card has an Open link to a filtered list.

Sidebar items for this group:

Item Opens Encoding queue Media list with encoding_queue=yes Failed encodings Media list with encoding_queue=fail Encodings One row for each encoding or chunk Captions Subtitle files Caption requests Whisper requests Trim requests Video trim jobs

docs.title: How encoding works
docs.text:
1. A video is uploaded. The original file is saved.
  2. MediaCMS reads the file with FFprobe.
  3. A video longer than CHUNKIZE_VIDEO_DURATION (300 seconds) is split into chunks of VIDEO_CHUNKS_DURATION (240 seconds).
  4. A Celery worker creates one Encoding for each chunk and each active encode profile.
  5. When all chunks of one resolution succeed, MediaCMS joins them into one final Encoding.
  6. MediaCMS creates the HLS version (.ts segments).

The final Encoding (chunk=False, status=success) is the file that the portal plays and offers for download.

All workers must use the same file system as the web server. This can be one host, NFS, or EFS.

docs.title: Encode profiles
docs.text:
Open Site > Encode profiles (/admin/files/encodeprofile/).

Field Values Name Free text Extension mp4, webm, gif Resolution 2160, 1440, 1080, 720, 480, 360, 240, 144 Codec h265, h264, vp9 Active On or off

To turn a resolution on or off:

  1. Open the profile.
  2. Clear or select Active.
  3. Select Save.

The change is used for new encodings. It does not change media that is already encoded.

Note

A profile named preview makes the hover preview. MediaCMS finds the preview by this name, not by the file extension. Do not rename it.

Warning

With no active profile, video does not encode. The Active encode profiles health check then fails.

The resolution list is fixed. A new resolution outside this list needs a code change.

docs.title: Find failed encodings
docs.text:
1. Open Processing > Failed encodings.
  2. Open a media row. Read the encoding logs.

The Site > Health page also warns about failed encodings, stale running encodings, and media with no encoding rows.

docs.title: Retry
docs.text:
Choose one action in the media list:

Action Use it to Generate missing encodings Create encodings that do not exist Force re-encode Encode again Regenerate thumbnails Make thumbnails again Regenerate sprites Make sprites again Regenerate preview Make the hover preview again Regenerate HLS Make the HLS files again Refresh all derivatives Run all of the above Refresh metadata / check integrity Read the file again and check it

In Processing > Encodings, the Retry failed encodings action retries the selected failed rows.

These actions need the original file. See Delete original file in Moderation.

docs.title: Stale encodings
docs.text: An encoding in the running state with no progress for RUNNING_STATE_STALE seconds is stale. The default is 7200 seconds (2 hours). The Health page lists stale encodings.

docs.title: FFmpeg settings
docs.text:
Set these in local_settings.py. A change needs a restart.

Setting Default Meaning FFMPEG_COMMAND ffmpeg Path to FFmpeg FFPROBE_COMMAND ffprobe Path to FFprobe FFMPEG_DEFAULT_PRESET medium H.264 speed and size trade-off. A slower preset gives smaller files and takes more time DO_NOT_TRANSCODE_VIDEO False True shows only the original video. No encoding runs CHUNKIZE_VIDEO_DURATION 300 Seconds. Longer videos are split into chunks VIDEO_CHUNKS_DURATION 240 Seconds in one chunk. Keep it smaller than CHUNKIZE_VIDEO_DURATION MINIMUM_RESOLUTIONS_TO_ENCODE [144, 240] Always encoded, even if this scales up MP4HLS_COMMAND Bento4 path Path to mp4hls SPRITE_NUM_SECS 10 Seconds between sprite images CELERY_SOFT_TIME_LIMIT 2 hours Soft time limit for Celery tasks

FFmpeg presets from fastest to slowest: ultrafast, superfast, veryfast, faster, fast, medium, slow, slower, veryslow.

Bitrates, CRF values, and codec parameters are in files/helpers.py.

Note

To change SPRITE_NUM_SECS, also change seconds in the frontend file frontend/src/static/js/components/media-viewer/VideoViewer/index.js. Then run make build-frontend.

To check the FFmpeg and FFprobe versions, open Site > System. See Site health and database.

docs.title: Whisper captions
docs.text: Whisper makes captions automatically. It runs only in the Docker installation with the full image.

docs.title: Turn it on
docs.text:
1. Use the mediacms/mediacms:full image for the celery_worker service. Or use docker-compose.full.yaml.
  2. Set USE_WHISPER_TRANSCRIBE = True in local_settings.py.
  3. Restart the services.
docker compose restart web celery_worker celery_beat

docs.title: Settings
docs.text: Setting Default Meaning USE_WHISPER_TRANSCRIBE False Turns the feature on USER_CAN_TRANSCRIBE_VIDEO True False limits caption requests to editors WHISPER_MODEL base The Whisper model name

docs.title: What happens
docs.text:
1. A user selects Transcription or English Translation on a video or audio media.
  2. MediaCMS creates a caption request (TranscriptionRequest) with status pending.
  3. The whisper_transcribe task runs in the long_tasks queue. The time limit is 2 hours.
  4. The task runs the whisper command with WHISPER_MODEL. A translation adds --task translate.
  5. MediaCMS saves the VTT file as a subtitle. The language is whisper (Transcription) or whisper-translation (English Translation).
  6. The request status changes to success or fail. The request log has the duration or the error.

docs.title: Check caption requests
docs.text:
1. Open Processing > Caption requests.
  2. Filter by status fail.
  3. Open a request. Read the log.

You can inspect or delete a request. Do not edit its parameters or log. The Health page warns about failed caption requests and about requests that succeeded with no subtitle.

docs.title: Trim requests
docs.text: A user trims a video from the media page. ALLOW_VIDEO_TRIMMER = False turns this off. Open Processing > Trim requests to see the jobs. The Health page warns about failed trim requests.

docs.title: MediaCMS Architecture
docs.text:
The web server writes jobs to Redis. Celery workers read them and write files to media_files.

flowchart LR
    upload["Upload"] --> web["web container"]
    web --> original[("Original file")]
    web --> redis[("Redis broker")]
    redis --> shortTasks["short_tasks worker"]
    redis --> longTasks["long_tasks worker"]
    longTasks --> ffmpeg["FFmpeg and FFprobe"]
    ffmpeg --> chunks["Chunk encodings"]
    chunks --> joined["Final encodings and HLS"]
    longTasks --> whisper["Whisper (full image only)"]
    whisper --> vtt["Subtitle VTT file"]
    joined --> mediaFiles[("media_files")]
    vtt --> mediaFiles
    profiles["Encode profiles"] --> longTasks
    adminPortal["Admin portal"] --> profiles
    adminPortal --> retry["Retry and regenerate actions"]
    retry --> redis

docs.title: SAML and identity providers
docs.text:
Use this page to add single sign-on to MediaCMS with SAML 2.0. The example uses Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure AD). The same steps apply to other SAML identity providers.

MediaCMS is the service provider (SP). Entra ID is the identity provider (IdP). The user's browser carries all messages between them. The MediaCMS server does not need inbound access from the Internet.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• You have admin access to MediaCMS and to Entra ID.
  • MediaCMS runs on HTTPS with a valid certificate.
  • You have a domain for MediaCMS. This page uses https://<MyMediaCMS.MyDomain.com>.
  • You chose a client ID name. For example, mediacms_entraid. You use the same name in both systems. It is part of the sign-in URL.

docs.title: Step 1: Turn on the MediaCMS settings
docs.text:
1. Open local_settings.py (deploy/docker/local_settings.py for Docker Compose).
  2. Add these lines.
USE_RBAC = True
USE_SAML = True
USE_IDENTITY_PROVIDERS = True

USE_X_FORWARDED_HOST = True
SECURE_PROXY_SSL_HEADER = ('HTTP_X_FORWARDED_PROTO', 'https')
SECURE_SSL_REDIRECT = True
CSRF_COOKIE_SECURE = True
SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE = True

SOCIALACCOUNT_ADAPTER = 'saml_auth.adapter.SAMLAccountAdapter'
SOCIALACCOUNT_PROVIDERS = {
    "saml": {
        "provider_class": "saml_auth.custom.provider.CustomSAMLProvider",
    }
}
  1. Restart the services. Do this before the next step.
docker compose restart web celery_worker celery_beat

Also set CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS to include your HTTPS host. The Site > Health page checks the proxy and cookie settings. See Site health and database.

The Integrations group now shows ID providers, login options, user accounts, user logs, and SAML configurations.

docs.title: Step 2: Create the application in Entra ID
docs.text:
1. Open the Azure portal. Open Enterprise Applications.
  2. Select New Application.
  3. Select Create your own application.
  4. Enter a name, for example MediaCMS.
  5. Select Integrate any other application you don't find in the gallery (Non-gallery).
  6. Select Create.

docs.title: Step 3: Set up SAML sign-on in Entra ID
docs.text:
1. Open the application. Under Manage, select Single sign-on.
  2. Select SAML.
  3. In Basic SAML Configuration, enter these values.
Field Value Identifier (Entity ID) https://<MyMediaCMS.MyDomain.com>/saml/metadata/ Reply URL (ACS URL) https://<MyMediaCMS.MyDomain.com>/accounts/saml/<MyClientID>/acs/ Sign-on URL https://<MyMediaCMS.MyDomain.com>/accounts/saml/<MyClientID>/login/ Relay State (optional) https://<MyMediaCMS.MyDomain.com>/ Logout URL (optional) https://<MyMediaCMS.MyDomain.com>/accounts/saml/<MyClientID>/sls/
  1. Select Save.
  2. Keep the Entra ID page open. You need values from it.

docs.title: Add a login option
docs.text:
1. Open the admin portal. Open Integrations > Login options.
  2. Select Add login option.
  3. Enter a Title. Users see this title on the sign-in page. For example, EntraID-SSO.
  4. Enter the Url: https://<MyMediaCMS.MyDomain.com>/accounts/saml/<MyClientID>/login/.

  7. Select Save.

Fill every attribute field. Enter NA where there is no value. A blank field causes a 500 error with Entra ID.

docs.text:
1. Open the application in Entra ID. Under Manage, select Users and Groups.

docs.title: Step 6: Test
docs.text:
1. Open the MediaCMS sign-in page in a private window.
  2. Select the login option. The browser goes to Microsoft.
  3. Sign in.
  4. Check that you return to MediaCMS signed in.
  5. Open Integrations > User logs. Read the SAML response log.
  6. Open Site > Health. Check the identity provider and SAML checks.

docs.title: Read the SAML response
docs.text:
1. Open the sign-in page. The browser goes to Microsoft.
  2. Before you sign in, press F12. Open the Network tab. Turn on Persistent Logging.
  3. Finish the sign-in.
  4. Find the POST request to https://<MyMediaCMS.MyDomain.com>/accounts/saml/<MyClientID>/acs/.
  5. Copy the SAMLResponse form value.
  6. Decode it with a From Base64 tool. Format the XML.

docs.title: Read the SP metadata
docs.text: Open https://<MyMediaCMS.MyDomain.com>/saml/metadata/ in a private window. Check that the XML has the values that you expect.

docs.title: Endless redirect loop
docs.text:
This happens when GLOBAL_LOGIN_REQUIRED is on and local sign-in is off. Django sends the user to the local sign-in page. That page is not available, so the user returns to the home page and the loop starts again.

  1. Open local_settings.py.
  2. Set LOGIN_URL to the SAML sign-in path.
LOGIN_URL = "/accounts/saml/mediacms_entraid/login/"
  1. Restart the services.

docs.title: Health checks
docs.text:
The Integrations page warns when:

  • USE_IDENTITY_PROVIDERS is on and there is no ID provider.
  • USE_IDENTITY_PROVIDERS is on and no login option is active.
  • USE_SAML is on and there is no SAML configuration.

See Integrations.

docs.title: MediaCMS Architecture
docs.text:
The browser carries the messages. MediaCMS and the IdP never connect to each other.

sequenceDiagram
    participant B as Browser
    participant M as MediaCMS
    participant E as Entra ID
    B->>M: Open /accounts/saml/CLIENT_ID/login/
    M->>B: Redirect with SAML request
    B->>E: Send SAML request
    E->>B: Sign-in page. User signs in
    E->>B: Signed SAMLResponse
    B->>M: POST /accounts/saml/CLIENT_ID/acs/
    M->>M: Check signature with IDP certificate
    M->>M: Create or find user. Apply role and group mappings
    M->>B: Signed-in session

docs.title: Site upgrade
docs.text:
Use this page to move an existing MediaCMS install to a new MediaCMS version. Use the upgrade_site command to check the old install before the upgrade.

Warning

A site upgrade is not a content migration. A site upgrade moves your own MediaCMS install to a new MediaCMS version. A content migration imports media from Kaltura, YouTube, or Panopto. For that job, read Content migration.

Only a superuser with server access can do a site upgrade. For the basic image update, see Update.

docs.title: What the tools do
docs.text:
Tool Changes the source database? Purpose upgrade_site inventory No. It only reads Reports what is different between the old install and the new image upgrade_site scratch No. It copies, then migrates the copy Proves that the migrations run on a copy of your data deploy/docker/postgres_gate.sh No. It only reads Compares a restored copy with its source deploy/docker/upgrade_site_smoke.sh No for the source. It writes to the scratch and empty databases Runs the whole check in one script upgrade_site apply Yes. It writes to the database it is connected to Applies your answers once, after the upgrade export_database No. It only reads Writes a database backup file

upgrade_site does not run prestart.sh. It never starts the migrations container.

docs.title: The three steps
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    old["Old install: database, tree, media"] --> inventory["inventory: read only report"]
    inventory --> decide{"Fast-forward and no problems?"}
    decide -->|"No"| stop["Stop. Fix the problem. Run inventory again"]
    decide -->|"Yes"| scratch["scratch: copy source and migrate the copy"]
    scratch --> check["Check the copy: gate and smoke script"]
    check --> upgrade["Upgrade: start the new image on the live database"]
    upgrade --> apply["apply: approval answer once and recount"]
    apply --> health["Site Health page"]
  1. Inventory. Read the report. The source is not changed.
  2. Scratch. Copy the source database and migrate the copy. The source is not changed.
  3. Apply. After the real upgrade, record your answers once.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
You need:

  • The new MediaCMS image.
  • The old install tree, mounted read-only at /audit/previous. Or set AUDIT_PREVIOUS to another path.
  • The old media tree, mounted read-only at /audit/media. Or set AUDIT_MEDIA to another path.
  • Connection URLs for PostgreSQL databases: the source, and an empty scratch database.
  • The pg_dump, pg_restore, and psql programs in the image.

Run the commands from the application directory (/home/mediacms.io/mediacms in the Docker image) in a one-off container of the new image. The application tree must stay the image code. Never mount the old tree on the application directory.

  1. Back up the source database with pg_dump.
  2. Copy the media_files directory.
  3. Keep the same SECRET_KEY. Credentials of content migrations are encrypted with a key derived from it.
  4. Point the settings of the one-off container at the source database. The Docker local_settings.py reads POSTGRES_NAME, POSTGRES_HOST, POSTGRES_PORT, POSTGRES_USER, and POSTGRES_PASSWORD.

docs.title: Step 1: Inventory
docs.text:
1. Run the command.
python manage.py upgrade_site inventory --previous /audit/previous
  1. Read the output. It is one line of JSON with three keys: migrations, checks, and reports.

The command reads django_migrations of the connected database. It compares those migrations with the migration files in the new image. Optionally, it also compares them with the migration files in the old tree.

docs.title: Read migrations
docs.text:
Key Meaning fast_forward true when every applied migration exists in the image problems List of migrations with a problem. Each has app, name, and reason pending Migrations in the image that are not applied yet Reason Meaning Action missing The database has a migration that the image does not have Stop. Use an image that has the migration do-not-fake The migration has the same name but different file content in the old tree and in the image Stop. Do not fake this migration. Ask for help

A do-not-fake problem is found only when the old tree is mounted. When fast_forward is false, do not continue to the upgrade.

docs.title: Read checks
docs.text:
checks reports data in the source database. A check with no rows is left out. The checks list can be empty.

Key Meaning listable Count of media where the stored listable value differs from the rule (public, encoding success, reviewed) approval Count of non-superuser accounts where is_approved is not true reports_public Count of public media with 10 or more reports reports_private Count of private media with at least one report reports_disagree Count of media where reported_times is not the number of report actions pages Pages with reserved slugs. blocked lists reserved slugs. copy lists slugs that can be kept

The report limit in this check is fixed at 10. It does not read REPORTED_TIMES_THRESHOLD.

docs.title: Read reports
docs.text:
reports describes the old install. MediaCMS does not rewrite any of this data.

Key Meaning templates Template files that are different in the old tree and in the image. Review your custom templates missing_media Count of stored media paths that are not in the mounted media tree. Shown only when the media tree is mounted rbac_grants Count of RBAC membership rows. They are kept as they are anonymous_pages Values of GLOBAL_LOGIN_REQUIRED, ALLOW_ANONYMOUS_ACTIONS, ALLOW_ANONYMOUS_USER_LISTING, and USERS_NEEDS_TO_BE_APPROVED that the old cms/local_settings.py sets

Note

Compare anonymous_pages with the new settings. Make sure that anonymous access in the new install is the same as before. See the Settings catalog.

docs.title: Step 2: Scratch
docs.text:
Use scratch to prove that the migrations run on a copy of your data.

  1. Create an empty PostgreSQL database for the copy.
  2. Run the command.
python manage.py upgrade_site scratch \
  --source-url postgres://USER:PASSWORD@SOURCE_HOST:5432/mediacms \
  --dest-url postgres://USER:PASSWORD@SCRATCH_HOST:5432/mediacms_scratch
  1. Read the last line. scratch restored and migrated means success.

The command does these things:

  1. It runs pg_dump --format=custom on the source.
  2. It runs pg_restore --no-owner into the scratch database.
  3. It runs python manage.py migrate --noinput for the scratch database only.

The destination URL must start with postgres:// or postgresql://. It needs a host and a database name. The command checks this after the restore. If a step fails, the command stops with an error. The source rows are not changed.

docs.title: Compare a restored copy with its source (optional)
docs.text:
The postgres_gate.sh script compares a restored copy with its source. Run it before any migration on the copy. scratch migrates the copy, so a gate after scratch can fail on django_migrations when migrations were pending.

  1. Restore a copy by hand.
pg_dump --format=custom --file /tmp/source.dump "$SOURCE_DATABASE_URL"
pg_restore --no-owner --dbname "$DEST_DATABASE_URL" /tmp/source.dump
  1. Run the gate.
SOURCE_DATABASE_URL=postgres://... DEST_DATABASE_URL=postgres://... \
  bash deploy/docker/postgres_gate.sh

The gate checks:

Check Tables or data Row counts files_media, users_user, files_page, django_migrations Sequences A hash of the sequence names and last values Keys A hash of the id values of files_media, users_user, and files_page No migration The gate does not change the count in django_migrations Result Meaning postgres gate ok All checks passed count mismatch <table>: <source> <dest> A table has a different row count sequence mismatch A sequence is different key mismatch <table> The id values are different Exit code 2 SOURCE_DATABASE_URL or DEST_DATABASE_URL is not set

docs.title: Run the whole check with one script
docs.text:
upgrade_site_smoke.sh runs the inventory, the scratch copy, an export round trip, and page checks.

  1. Set the variables.
Variable Needed Meaning SOURCE_DATABASE_URL Yes The source database DEST_DATABASE_URL Yes The scratch database EMPTY_DATABASE_URL Yes A second, empty database for the export round trip AUDIT_PREVIOUS No Old tree. The default is /audit/previous AUDIT_MEDIA No Old media tree. The default is /audit/media
  1. Run the script.
bash deploy/docker/upgrade_site_smoke.sh
  1. Read the last line. upgrade_site smoke ok means success.

The script does these things in order:

  1. It refuses to run when the old tree is mounted on the application directory.
  2. It counts django_migrations in the source, runs inventory, and counts again. The counts must be equal.
  3. When .secret_key exists in the old tree, it checks that inventory did not change the file.
  4. It checks that the media tree is mounted.
  5. It runs scratch. Then it checks that the source django_migrations count did not change.
  6. It writes a backup with export_database. It restores that file into the empty database. It compares the row counts of files_media, users_user, and files_page.
  7. On the scratch database, anonymous /, /about, and /latest must return 200. The sign-in page /accounts/login/ must show a password field.
  8. On the scratch database, it creates two test users: audit-editor and audit-pending. The editor must open /manage/media. The pending user must open /. The pending user must get 403 for an upload to /api/v1/media.

The script does not call postgres_gate.sh. Run the gate by hand if you want it.

docs.title: Step 3: Upgrade and apply
docs.text:
1. Update the image and start the containers. See Update. The migrations container runs migrate.
  2. Open Site > Health. Fix failures.
  3. Run apply once, with your answers.
python manage.py upgrade_site apply --choice approve --recount

apply needs at least one of --choice or --recount. Without them it stops with an error.

Option Effect --choice approve Marks all existing pending accounts as approved. Only non-superusers with is_approved false or empty --choice leave Does not change any account. Records that you chose to leave them --recount Sets media_count of each category and tag from public, reviewed media

Output examples: approval approve 12 and recount 3. The number is the count of changed rows.

Run apply only after the upgrade. The UpgradeDecision table comes from migration 0022_upgradedecision.

docs.title: The approval answer is used once
docs.text:
apply --choice stores the answer in the UpgradeDecision table. The row has the key approval, your choice, and applied.

  • The first call applies the answer and sets applied to true.
  • A later call changes no account. This is true for approve and for leave. The count is 0.
  • A new pending account that arrives later stays pending.

To read the stored answer:

python manage.py shell -c "from files.models import UpgradeDecision; print(list(UpgradeDecision.objects.values()))"

There is no admin page for UpgradeDecision.

--recount can run again. A second run changes nothing when the counts are right.

docs.title: Reserved page slugs
docs.text:
Page slugs decide the public address of a custom page. These names are reserved. They are used by MediaCMS routes:

accounts, login, logout, signup, password, saml, approval_required, api, api-auth, swagger, docs, admin, lti, tinymce, fu, manage, user, channel

A page cannot be saved with a reserved slug. The save raises an error. A page that was created with a reserved slug in an old install is not served as a public page. The inventory pages check lists these pages in blocked. It does not put them in the copy list.

To fix a blocked page:

  1. Open Site > Pages.
  2. Open the blocked page.
  3. Change Slug to an allowed value.
  4. Select Save.

See Custom pages and appearance for the full slug rules.

docs.title: If something fails
docs.text: Problem What to do fast_forward is false Do not upgrade. Fix the problems list first scratch stops in pg_dump or pg_restore Check the URLs, the passwords, and the PostgreSQL client version scratch stops in migrate Read the migration error. The source is not changed. Fix the cause and run scratch with a new empty database Smoke script reports a count change Stop. Do not upgrade. The source django_migrations changed postgres gate reports a mismatch The copy is not the same as the source. Restore the copy again Version 2 data directory PostgreSQL 13 data does not start on a newer PostgreSQL. See Update

docs.title: MediaCMS Architecture
docs.text:
The check tools read the old install and write only to scratch databases. The upgrade uses the live database.

flowchart TD
    sourceDb[("Source database")] -->|"read only"| inventory["upgrade_site inventory"]
    oldTree["Old tree /audit/previous"] -->|"read only"| inventory
    oldMedia["Old media /audit/media"] -->|"read only"| inventory
    imageCode["New image code"] --> inventory
    inventory --> report["JSON report: migrations, checks, reports"]
    sourceDb -->|"pg_dump"| scratch["upgrade_site scratch"]
    scratch -->|"pg_restore then migrate"| scratchDb[("Scratch database")]
    sourceDb -.->|"compare"| gate["postgres_gate.sh"]
    scratchDb -.-> gate
    scratchDb --> smoke["upgrade_site_smoke.sh page checks"]

docs.title: Site health and database
docs.text:
Use this page to check the health of the portal, read configuration and system facts, back up the database, and read the Celery task list.

The Site group has four pages. Each page is a dashboard section.

Page URL Health /admin/dashboard/health/ Configuration /admin/dashboard/configuration/ System /admin/dashboard/system/ Database /admin/dashboard/database/

docs.title: Health
docs.text:
The Health page shows four counters and one table.

Counter Meaning Passing checks Checks with status OK Warnings Checks that need attention Failures Checks that must be fixed Info checks Facts. No action needed

The Health checks table has the columns Status, Check, and Detail. A check name with a link opens the list that has the problem.

  1. Open Site > Health.
  2. Read the Failures counter. Fix failures first.
  3. Open the Health checks table. Read each warning.
  4. Select the check name to open the filtered list.
  5. Fix the problem.
  6. Select Refresh stats. Check that the check now shows OK.

The table shows Copy tools. Use them to paste the table into a ticket.

docs.title: What the checks cover
docs.text:
Area Examples Site record Django site record exists. Site name matches PORTAL_NAME. Site domain matches FRONTEND_HOST Hosts ALLOWED_HOSTS includes the FRONTEND_HOST host. FRONTEND_HOST uses HTTPS. DEBUG is off Services Cache and Redis are reachable. An active superuser exists Email DEFAULT_FROM_EMAIL is set. EMAIL_USE_TLS and EMAIL_USE_SSL are not both on Encoding Active encode profiles exist. Encoding failures. Encode, trim, and caption job failures Integrity Listable flag mismatch. Video success with no encodings. Queued video with no encoding rows. Stale running encodings. Duplicate md5sum. Duplicate names. Missing media metadata. Recent integrity warnings Reverse proxy USE_X_FORWARDED_HOST, SECURE_PROXY_SSL_HEADER, CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS, secure cookies, SECURE_SSL_REDIRECT, CORS allow-all Storage MEDIA_ROOT, HLS_DIR, and TEMP_DIRECTORY can be read and written. The sub-directories for original, encoded, upload, and chunk files can be read and written Workflow Open reports. Reports above the limit. Media waiting for review. Users waiting for approval. Inactive users Integrations See Integrations

The reverse-proxy checks apply when FRONTEND_HOST starts with https. For a local or DEBUG install, a gap is shown as Info. For a production install, a gap is shown as Warning.

A storage check writes and then deletes one small file in the directory. It never creates a directory.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
The Configuration page lists the main settings as they are now. It is read-only. It shows PORTAL_NAME, FRONTEND_HOST, PORTAL_WORKFLOW, MEDIA_IS_REVIEWED, CAN_ADD_MEDIA, CAN_COMMENT, USERS_NEEDS_TO_BE_APPROVED, GLOBAL_LOGIN_REQUIRED, ACCOUNT_EMAIL_VERIFICATION, the email TLS and SSL switches, the USE_* switches, LOCAL_INSTALL, and DEBUG. It also shows the reverse-proxy and path values.

To change a value, edit local_settings.py. See the Settings catalog.

docs.title: System
docs.text:
The System page shows facts for troubleshooting.

Group Examples MediaCMS installation Version, install type, operating system, git branch and commit Python Executable, version, prefix Packages Django, Celery, psycopg, redis versions Process PID, user, working directory, settings module, time zone, DEBUG Database Engine and server version Cache and Celery Cache backend. Broker URL without user name or password Binaries FFmpeg and FFprobe path and version Paths BASE_DIR, MEDIA_ROOT, PATH, sys.path Environment Variable names. Only a short allowlist shows a value. Other variables show (set) or (empty)

docs.title: Database
docs.text:
The Database page shows PostgreSQL facts for the connected database.

Part What it shows Counters and checks Connection use, idle sessions, long-running sessions, transaction ID age, cache hit ratio, deadlocks, temporary files, checkpoint balance, replication lag Object totals Row counts for the main models, with links Database backup A download button Database restore An upload form (superuser)

Check limits:

Check Warning Failure Connection use 70 percent of the maximum 90 percent Transaction ID age 200 million 1.5 billion Cache hit ratio Under 99 percent Under 90 percent Replication lag 30 seconds 300 seconds

The cache hit check shows Info until 1000 blocks are read.

docs.title: Back up the database
docs.text:
Only a superuser can download a backup.

  1. Open Site > Database.
  2. Find the Database backup card.
  3. Select Download a database backup.

The file is a gzipped JSON fixture. The name is mediacms-database-backup-YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM.json.gz.

Warning

The file does not contain uploaded media files. It has only their stored paths. Back up the media_files directory too.

Note

This backup leaves out operational rows: sessions, admin log entries, notifications, identity provider user logs, LTI launch logs, trim requests, and caption requests. It also leaves out likes, dislikes, watches, ratings, and failed encodings. For a full copy of the database, also use pg_dump.

To write the same file from a terminal, use export_database:

python manage.py export_database --output /tmp/backup.json.gz
Option Effect --output PATH Required. The file to write --include-engagement Adds likes, dislikes, watches, and ratings --include-noisy-status Adds failed encodings, trim requests, and caption requests

The backup stores which options were used. Restore reads this.

docs.title: Restore a database backup
docs.text:
A restore is possible only on an initial installation. Use it to move data to a new, empty install of the same MediaCMS version.

Before you start, check these conditions. If one is not true, the page shows a list of reasons and turns the restore off:

  • There is exactly one user. The user is an active superuser.
  • There is at most one channel. It is the default channel.
  • The categories and encode profiles are the ones from the first install.
  • There is exactly one site record.

  • No other model has rows.

  • Sign in as the superuser of the new install.

  • Open Site > Database.
  • Find the Database restore card.
  • Select the file in Backup file.
  • Select Restore database backup.
  • Confirm the question.
  • Sign in with an account from the backup.

The file size limit is 64 MiB compressed and 256 MiB after unzip. The restore runs in one transaction. A bad file changes nothing.

Note

Permissions and content types stay as created by migrations. Use a backup from the same MediaCMS version. Copy the media_files directory to the new install by hand.

For a site upgrade, read Site upgrade.

docs.title: Get Support
docs.text:
Open /admin/dashboard/support/. Select Download support bundle and then Download as text or Download as Markdown. Or select Copy text or Copy Markdown.

The file lists the version, the health warnings and failures, and the system rows. Secrets are omitted or redacted. It is safe to paste into a GitHub issue.

docs.title: Task list API
docs.text:
/api/v1/tasks lists the Celery tasks that are running or waiting.

Item Value Method GET Path /api/v1/tasks (also /api/v1/tasks/) Who Staff (IsAdminUser) Documented in Swagger No

The response has these keys:

Key Content active tasks: tasks that a worker runs now reserved tasks: tasks that a worker has taken scheduled tasks: tasks with a start time task_ids All task IDs media_profile_pairs Pairs of media friendly token and profile ID for encode_media tasks

Each task has worker, task_id, args, name, and time_start. An encode_media task also has info with profile name, media title, and encoding progress.

Example with a session cookie or basic authentication:

curl -u admin:PASSWORD https://portal.example.org/api/v1/tasks

Warning

DELETE /api/v1/tasks/<token> does not cancel a task. It returns 204 and does nothing. To stop encoding work, stop the worker or use the actions in Processing.

The call asks the workers over Redis. It needs at least one running worker. If no worker answers, the request can fail with a server error.

Use these guides when you change the MediaCMS code. You run MediaCMS on your computer, write code, run tests, and add documentation.

docs.title: MediaCMS Architecture
docs.text:
A developer works on three parts: the Django backend, the React frontend, and the Celery workers. Docker runs all of them for you.

flowchart LR

    compose --> web["web: Django runserver, port 80"]

Read Architecture for the full stack.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
1. Install Docker and Docker Compose.
  2. Clone the repository.
  3. Read AGENTS.md in the repository root. It lists the rules for code style and commits.
  4. Read the Code of Conduct.

docs.title: Rules for every change
docs.text:
• Run pre-commit run --all before you commit. It runs black, isort, and flake8 for Python.
  • Use Conventional Commit messages: feat, fix, chore, docs, style, refactor, perf, test, depr.
  • Do not change the version in package.json. Releases are automatic.
  • Do not edit CHANGELOG.md. Releases are automatic.
  • Do not edit cms/settings.py for a deployment. Put overrides in cms/local_settings.py.
  • Add every new interface text to files/frontend_translations/en.py first. See Translations.

Note

This documentation is for the developer of MediaCMS. To run a production site, read the Admin guides and the Deploy guide.

docs.title: Add a documentation page
docs.text: Use this guide to add a page to this documentation site, build the site, and add a language.

docs.title: MediaCMS Architecture
docs.text:
The site is built with MkDocs. Source pages are Markdown files in docs/en/. Some pages are generated from the repository by scripts. The build puts the result in site/.

flowchart LR
    md["docs/en/*.md pages"] --> mkdocs["mkdocs build --strict"]
    nav["mkdocs.yml: nav"] --> mkdocs
    prep["scripts/prepare_docs_build.py"] -->|"writes generated pages"| md
    pkg["package.json and CHANGELOG.md"] --> prep
    api["manage.py generate_swagger"] --> openapi["docs/en/reference/openapi.yaml"]
    openapi --> mkdocs
    py["Python source: files, cms"] -->|"mkdocstrings"| mkdocs
    mkdocs --> site["site/"]
    check["scripts/check_doc_scenarios.py"] -->|"checks"| scen["docs/en/scenarios/*.md"]
    lang["scripts/add_docs_language.py"] --> langs["docs/locale/ and mkdocs.yml i18n"]

For the full stack of MediaCMS itself, see Architecture.

docs.title: Install the tools
docs.text:
1. Create a Python virtual environment.

  2. Install the documentation tools:

    pip install -r requirements-docs.txt

docs.title: Add a page
docs.text:
1. Choose the folder. Use the section that matches the reader:

    Folder Reader docs/en/getting-started/ New installers docs/en/roles/ One role docs/en/guides/user/, operator/, admin/, developer/ One guide set docs/en/scenarios/ One role on one path docs/en/reference/ Reference pages

  2. Create the file, for example docs/en/guides/developer/my-topic.md.

  3. Start the file with one # heading. Use a short title.
  4. Write the page. Follow the Writing guide.
  5. Add a MediaCMS Architecture heading to each task guide and each role page. Add a Mermaid diagram if the task crosses more than one part of the system. Do not repeat this heading in a scenario.
  6. Link to other pages with a relative path to the .md file, for example [Tests](tests.md).
  7. Open mkdocs.yml.

  8. Add the page under nav: in the right section:

    - Developer:
    - guides/developer/index.md
    - Local development: guides/developer/local-dev.md
    - My topic: guides/developer/my-topic.md

    The path is relative to docs/en/. A path without a label uses the page title.

  9. Link the new page from the index.md of its folder.

  10. Build the site. See Build the site.

Warning

A page that is not in nav: is built but is not in the menu. mkdocs build --strict reports a broken link as an error.

docs.title: Write the page
docs.text:
Follow these rules. The Writing guide has the full list.

  • Use simple, short sentences in the active voice.
  • Use one word for one thing. Check the glossary.
  • Number the steps. Put one action in each step. Start each step with a verb.
  • Put notes and warnings in admonitions (!!! note, !!! warning).
  • Write interface labels in bold, as they appear on the screen.
  • Keep setting names, commands, and paths in backticks.
  • Use Manage pages for /manage/... and admin portal for /admin/. Do not mix them.

Use Mermaid in a fenced block:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    a["Browser"] --> b["Django"]
```

Quote each label that has spaces or punctuation.

docs.title: Generated pages
docs.text:
Do not edit these files. scripts/prepare_docs_build.py writes them and each file starts with a generated by comment.

  • docs/en/reference/this-version.md
  • docs/en/reference/whats-new.md
  • docs/en/reference/changelog.md
  • docs/en/reference/api.md
  • docs/en/reference/openapi.yaml (a stub if CI did not export it)
  • docs/en/languages.md

To change them, change the script or the source data (package.json, CHANGELOG.md, docs/languages.yml).

docs.title: Reference pages
docs.text:
• docs/en/reference/python.md uses mkdocstrings. Add a line module.path.name to document a function or class. The setting paths: [.] in mkdocs.yml lets mkdocstrings find the modules from the repository root.
  • docs/en/reference/node.md has a manual table of frontend entry points. Update the table when you add a file to frontend/src/entries/.

docs.title: Prepare the build
docs.text:
Run the prepare script before each build:

python scripts/prepare_docs_build.py

The script does these things:

  1. Reads the version from package.json.
  2. Writes reference/this-version.md, reference/whats-new.md, and reference/changelog.md.
  3. Writes languages.md from docs/languages.yml.
  4. Creates reference/openapi.yaml as a stub if the file is missing. Then it writes reference/api.md.
  5. Copies docs/_shared/stylesheets/ and docs/_shared/assets/ into each locale folder that builds.

To export the real OpenAPI schema, run this before the prepare script:

DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE=cms.docs_settings SECRET_KEY=docs-build-not-a-secret \
  python manage.py generate_swagger -f yaml -o docs/en/reference/openapi.yaml

cms/docs_settings.py uses an in-memory SQLite database, so no PostgreSQL is needed.

docs.title: Check scenarios
docs.text:
If you add or change a page in docs/en/scenarios/, run the scenario check:

python scripts/check_doc_scenarios.py

The script checks each scenario file for:

  • Front matter with the keys id, role, audience, and goal.
  • A related_tests list. Each entry must be an existing test file or file::function. An empty list needs coverage: gap.
  • A screenshot placeholder <figure> where the alt text and the <figcaption> text are the same sentence.

Use the scenario template to start a scenario.

docs.title: Build the site
docs.text:
1. Run the prepare script:

    python scripts/prepare_docs_build.py

  2. Run the scenario check:

    python scripts/check_doc_scenarios.py

  3. Build the site. Fix every warning, because --strict makes warnings errors:

    mkdocs build --strict

  4. To read the site in a browser, run mkdocs serve. Open http://127.0.0.1:8000.

The CI workflow .github/workflows/docs.yml runs the same steps on each pull request.

docs.title: Add a language
docs.text:
1. Open docs/languages.yml. Find the locale code. The codes match LANGUAGES in cms/settings.py.

  2. Run the script:

    python scripts/add_docs_language.py fr

    Replace fr with your locale code.

  3. Check the result. The script does these things:

    • Sets build: true for the locale in docs/languages.yml.
    • Creates docs/<locale>/index.md if it does not exist.
    • Adds the locale to plugins.i18n.languages in mkdocs.yml.

  4. Copy a page from docs/en/ to the same path under docs/<locale>/.

  5. Translate the sentences. Keep UI labels in bold as the English words on the product screen.
  6. Run the prepare script and mkdocs build --strict.

A page that you did not translate falls back to the English page.

Note

The script stops with Unknown locale if the code is not in docs/languages.yml. Add the code there first.

docs.title: Request path
docs.text:
1. The browser asks nginx for a page.
  2. nginx sends page and API requests to gunicorn. nginx serves static files and media files by itself.
  3. Django picks a view from cms/urls.py and the URL files of each app.
  4. The view reads or writes PostgreSQL and Redis.
  5. A Django template makes the page. The template loads a React bundle from static/js/.
  6. React calls the REST API under /api/v1/ to get data.

In the development stack there is no nginx and no gunicorn. runserver serves the pages. The webpack dev server on port 8088 proxies to runserver. See Local development.

docs.title: Django apps
docs.text:
All apps are listed in INSTALLED_APPS in cms/settings.py.

App Folder What it holds Project cms/ settings.py, urls.py, celery.py, permissions.py (REST permission classes), dev_settings.py, test_settings.py. Files files/ The main app. Models for media, category, comment, encoding, playlist, subtitle, and page. Views, serializers, forms, Celery tasks (tasks.py), helper functions (methods.py), management commands, and frontend_translations/. Users users/ The User model. It has the flags is_editor and is_manager. It also has the RBAC access methods. RBAC rbac/ RBACGroup and RBACMembership. Roles are member, contributor, and manager. Migration service migrationservice/ Content migration from other platforms: models, providers, scheduling, Celery tasks, and views. Admin customizations admin_customizations/ Extra pages for the admin portal: health, database stats, processing stats, backup, restore, and the support bundle.

Other apps in INSTALLED_APPS are actions (user actions such as watch and like), identity_providers, lti, saml_auth, and uploader.

docs.title: Data stores
docs.text:
Store Use PostgreSQL All records: users, media, encodings, comments, playlists, RBAC groups. Redis The Django cache and the Celery broker and result backend. Media folder Original files, encoded files, chunks, HLS files, thumbnails, and previews.

Warning

All Celery workers and the web server must see the same media folder. Use the same machine or a shared file system such as NFS or EFS.

docs.title: Celery tasks and queues
docs.text:
Celery tasks are in files/tasks.py and migrationservice/tasks.py. Each task goes to one of two queues.

Queue Used for Examples short_tasks Quick tasks chunkize_media, media_init, update_search_vector, video_trim_task, state checks long_tasks Slow tasks encode_media, create_hls, whisper_transcribe, produce_sprite_from_video

celery beat runs scheduled tasks. The schedule is CELERY_BEAT_SCHEDULE in cms/settings.py.

In tests, TESTING=True sets CELERY_TASK_ALWAYS_EAGER. Tasks then run as plain functions. See Tests.

docs.title: Encode pipeline
docs.text:
The pipeline turns an uploaded video into files that users can play. The database model is Encoding in files/models/encoding.py. Each Encoding belongs to one media item and one EncodeProfile. Profiles are set in the admin portal at /admin/files/encodeprofile/.

flowchart TD
    upload["Upload creates Media"] --> init["media_init task"]
    init --> encode_call["Media.encode"]
    encode_call --> long_q{"Duration more than CHUNKIZE_VIDEO_DURATION?"}
    long_q -->|"No"| direct["One Encoding for each profile: chunk is False"]
    long_q -->|"Yes"| chunkize["chunkize_media task: split with FFmpeg"]
    chunkize --> chunk_enc["One Encoding for each chunk and profile: chunk is True"]
    direct --> encode_task["encode_media task on long_tasks"]
    chunk_enc --> encode_task
    encode_task --> chunk_done{"Is this a chunk with status success?"}
    chunk_done -->|"No"| final_enc["Encoding status success"]
    chunk_done -->|"Yes"| all_chunks{"All chunks of this profile done?"}
    all_chunks -->|"No"| wait["Wait for other chunks"]
    all_chunks -->|"Yes"| concat["Join chunks into one Encoding: chunk is False, status success"]
    concat --> final_enc
    final_enc --> post["Media.post_encode_actions"]
    post --> hls["create_hls task: .ts segments, h264 only"]
    post --> listable["Update encoding_status and listable"]

Follow these facts when you work on the pipeline:

  • A video longer than CHUNKIZE_VIDEO_DURATION is split into chunks. The default is 5 minutes (60 * 5). Each chunk is about VIDEO_CHUNKS_DURATION. The default is 4 minutes (60 * 4). VIDEO_CHUNKS_DURATION must be smaller than CHUNKIZE_VIDEO_DURATION.
  • chunkize_media creates one Encoding for each chunk and each profile. These have chunk=True.
  • The preview profile is not split. It is encoded from the original file.
  • When all chunks of one profile have status success, the post_save signal in files/models/encoding.py joins them into one Encoding with chunk=False and status='success'. It then removes the chunk files.
  • Only the joined Encoding is served and downloaded.
  • A short video skips the chunk step. It gets one Encoding for each profile.
  • create_hls runs after a successful, non-chunk h264 encoding. It writes HLS segments (.ts files) in HLS_DIR.
  • A profile with a resolution higher than the original video is skipped. The exception is the resolutions in MINIMUM_RESOLUTIONS_TO_ENCODE.

Note

Some older notes call the model Encode. The class name in the code is Encoding.

docs.title: Media becomes listable
docs.text:
Media.save in files/models/media.py sets listable each time. The value is true only when all of these are true:

  • state == "public"
  • encoding_status == "success"
  • is_reviewed is True

See Python reference.

docs.title: React frontend
docs.text:
React is a library that Django templates load. It is not a single-page application and it has no router.

Part Path What it does Entry files frontend/src/entries/<name>.js One file for each page. It calls renderPage with a page component. Pages frontend/src/static/js/pages/ Page components. Components frontend/src/static/js/components/ Shared interface parts. Build frontend/webpack.config.js Makes static/js/<name>.js for each entry. Django templates templates/cms/*.html Load static/js/<name>.js and static/js/_commons.js.

Example: frontend/src/entries/media.js becomes static/js/media.js. The template templates/cms/media.html loads it. See Node reference for the full table.

docs.title: Admin and Manage surfaces
docs.text:
Two surfaces use this stack in different ways. Do not mix them.

  • Manage pages (/manage/media, /manage/users, /manage/comments) are React pages. They call the REST API. Editors and managers use them.
  • Admin portal (/admin/) is the Django admin with Jazzmin. admin_customizations/ adds pages to it. Staff and superusers use it.
