docs.title: Local development
docs.text: Use this guide to run MediaCMS on your computer with Docker. It uses the file docker-compose-dev.yaml.

docs.title: MediaCMS Architecture
docs.text:
The development stack runs six services by default. The optional docs profile adds an MkDocs watcher. The web service runs the Django development server. The frontend service runs the webpack development server. Both servers use the same repository folder.

flowchart LR
    browser80["Browser: http://localhost"] --> web["web: Django runserver, port 80"]
    browser8088["Browser: http://localhost:8088"] --> frontend["frontend: webpack dev server, port 8088"]
    browserDocs["Browser: /documentation/"] --> web
    frontend -->|"proxy pages and API to MEDIACMS_BACKEND=http://web"| web
    web --> db[("db: PostgreSQL 17")]
    web --> redis[("redis")]
    migrations["migrations: prestart.sh"] --> db
    worker["celery_worker"] --> db
    worker --> redis
    docs["docs profile: mkdocs → site/"] -.-> web
    repo[["Repository folder, mounted into web, migrations, celery_worker, and docs"]] -.-> web

For the full stack, see Architecture.

docs.title: Services
docs.text:
Service What it does migrations Runs deploy/docker/prestart.sh. It runs database migrations and creates the admin user. web Runs python manage.py runserver 0.0.0.0:80. It reloads when Python files change. frontend Runs npm install && npm run start in frontend/. It starts the webpack dev server. db PostgreSQL 17. redis Cache and Celery broker. celery_worker Runs Celery tasks, such as video encoding. docs (optional profile) Builds MkDocs into site/ and rebuilds when files change. Off by default.

In this stack Django runs in debug mode with Django Debug Toolbar. It does not run gunicorn or nginx. corsheaders allows all origins.

docs.title: Ports
docs.text:
URL What you see http://localhost (port 80) The real Django site. It serves the built frontend bundles from static/. http://localhost:8088 The webpack development server. It proxies all pages and API calls to Django. It serves the live frontend bundles. http://localhost/documentation/ The MkDocs site (same origin as the portal). Requires the optional docs profile.

Use port 8088 when you edit the frontend. Use port 80 to check what users see.

docs.title: Start the stack
docs.text:
1. Install Docker and Docker Compose.
  2. Open a terminal in the repository root.

  3. Build the images:

    docker compose -f docker-compose-dev.yaml build

  4. Start the services:

    docker compose -f docker-compose-dev.yaml up

  5. Wait a few minutes. The first start installs frontend packages and runs migrations.

  6. Open http://localhost.
  7. Sign in with user admin and password admin.

docs.title: Documentation on the same site
docs.text:
Django serves the built MkDocs site at http://localhost/documentation/ when DEVELOPMENT_MODE is on. The optional docs Compose profile builds into site/ and watches for changes.

  1. Start the documentation watcher:

    make docs-up

  2. Wait for the first build to finish. Check the logs with make docs-logs.

  3. Open http://localhost/documentation/.

One-shot build without watching:

make docs-build

Stop the watcher with make docs-down. The path /docs/ stays reserved for ReDoc at /docs/api/ and for page slugs.

docs.title: Change Python code
docs.text:
1. Edit the Python files.
  2. Check http://localhost. Django reloads by itself.

If Django stops because of an error, such as a SyntaxError, fix the error. Then restart the service:

docker compose -f docker-compose-dev.yaml restart web

Warning

A change to a setting needs a restart. Restart all three services that read settings:

docker compose -f docker-compose-dev.yaml restart web celery_worker

The development stack has no celery_beat service. Restart celery_beat only on a stack that has it.

docs.title: Change frontend code
docs.text:
React is a library that Django templates load. It is not a separate single-page application. Django owns the routes, the pages, the data, and the login.

The code is in two places:

  • frontend/src/ holds the React code.
  • templates/ holds the Django templates. All templates extend templates/root.html.

Each page has an entry file frontend/src/entries/<name>.js. The template for the page loads static/js/<name>.js and static/js/_commons.js. See Node reference for the list of entries.

  1. Edit the files in frontend/src/.
  2. Open http://localhost:8088. The page reloads when you save.

  3. Build the bundles for port 80:

    make build-frontend

  4. Open http://localhost. Check the change.

  5. Commit the changes in static/ together with the changes in frontend/src/.

make build-frontend runs these commands:

docker compose -f docker-compose-dev.yaml exec frontend npm run dist
cp -r frontend/dist/static/* static/
docker compose -f docker-compose-dev.yaml restart web

Note

Port 80 does not show frontend changes until you build. Port 8088 and port 80 can look different. This is normal.

docs.title: Styles
docs.text:
• Put styles for more than one page in static/css/_commons.css.
  • Put styles for one page in static/css/<name>.css. The template of that page must link the file.

The webpack build is set in frontend/webpack.config.js. It makes one bundle for each file in frontend/src/entries/.

docs.title: Run commands in a container
docs.text:
Open a shell in the web container:

docker compose -f docker-compose-dev.yaml exec web /bin/bash

Then run Django commands in the shell:

python manage.py shell

The shortcut make admin-shell does the same. It needs the web container.

Warning

The admin-shell target in the Makefile runs docker compose ps -q web without -f docker-compose-dev.yaml. If you start the stack with -f docker-compose-dev.yaml, the shortcut can report Web container not found. Use the docker compose -f docker-compose-dev.yaml exec web /bin/bash command above.

docs.title: Make targets
docs.text:
Run these from the repository root. The development stack must be running.

Target What it runs make build-frontend Builds the frontend, copies it to static/, restarts web. make test Backend tests with pytest -n auto and TESTING=True. make test-coverage Backend tests with coverage. make test-frontend Frontend Jest tests in CI mode. make test-frontend-coverage Frontend Jest tests with coverage. make admin-shell Shell in the web container.

See Tests for the test commands.

docs.title: Check the code style
docs.text:
1. Install the hook once: pre-commit install.
  2. Run all checks: pre-commit run --all.
  3. Fix every problem the checks report.

Python uses black, isort (profile black), and flake8. The frontend uses Prettier. The Prettier settings are in .prettierrc.

docs.title: Fake media for development
docs.text: The web service sets ALLOW_POPULATE_FAKE_MEDIA to True. This allows the management command populate_fake_media.

docs.title: Stop the stack
docs.text:
1. Press Ctrl+C in the terminal that runs up.

  2. Remove the containers when you no longer need them:

    docker compose -f docker-compose-dev.yaml down

Note

The database files are in ../postgres_data, next to the repository folder. down does not delete them.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text: Use this guide to run the backend tests (pytest) and the frontend tests (Jest).

docs.title: MediaCMS Architecture
docs.text:
Backend tests run inside the web container. They use cms/test_settings.py. Frontend tests run inside the frontend container.

flowchart LR
    make["make test"] --> web["web container: pytest"]
    web --> settings["cms/test_settings.py"]
    settings --> eager["CELERY_TASK_ALWAYS_EAGER = True"]
    settings --> tmpmedia["Temporary MEDIA_ROOT"]
    web --> conftest["conftest.py: network block, cache clear"]
    web --> testdb[("PostgreSQL test database")]
    makefe["make test-frontend"] --> fe["frontend container: Jest"]
    fe --> jsdom["jsdom test environment"]

For the full stack, see Architecture.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
1. Start the development stack. See Local development.
  2. Wait until the web and db services are ready.

docs.title: Backend tests
docs.text:
Warning

Always set TESTING=True. Without it, Celery tasks go to a broker that does not run in tests. TESTING=True makes Celery run tasks as plain functions.

docs.title: Run all tests in parallel
docs.text:
make test

This runs:

docker compose -f docker-compose-dev.yaml exec --env TESTING=True -T web pytest -n auto

-n auto uses pytest-xdist to run tests on all CPU cores.

docs.title: Run all tests in one process
docs.text:
docker compose -f docker-compose-dev.yaml exec --env TESTING=True -T web pytest

Use this when you debug a failing test. It prints output in order.

docs.title: Run one file or one test
docs.text:
docker compose -f docker-compose-dev.yaml exec --env TESTING=True -T web pytest tests/test_fixtures.py
docker compose -f docker-compose-dev.yaml exec --env TESTING=True -T web pytest tests/api/test_api_permissions.py -k upload

docs.title: Run with coverage
docs.text:
make test-coverage

This runs pytest -n auto --cov --cov-report=term --cov-report=html. The settings for coverage are in .coveragerc. Migrations, tests, and the frontend are not counted.

docs.title: Test settings
docs.text:
pytest.ini sets DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE = cms.test_settings. This file does these things:

  • Sets TESTING to True if it is not set.
  • Sets CELERY_TASK_ALWAYS_EAGER = True.
  • Uses a temporary MEDIA_ROOT and a temporary HLS_DIR.
  • Uses a local memory cache and a fast password hasher.
  • Sets MEDIA_IS_REVIEWED = True, USERS_NEEDS_TO_BE_APPROVED = False, and USE_IDENTITY_PROVIDERS = False.
  • Uses the test database test_mediacms.

The norecursedirs setting in pytest.ini skips frontend, static, media_files, logs, and docs.

docs.title: conftest.py
docs.text:
conftest.py in the repository root does these things:

  • Blocks network access. It replaces socket.getaddrinfo. A test can only reach localhost, 127.0.0.1, ::1, 0.0.0.0, the database host, the Redis host, and the broker host. Any other host raises socket.gaierror.
  • Cleans up. After the run it deletes the temporary media folder.
  • Clears the cache. An automatic fixture clears the cache before each test.

Do not write a test that calls an outside service. Replace the call with a mock.

docs.title: Test folders
docs.text:
Folder What it tests tests/api/ REST API: media, categories, comments, playlists, permissions, search, login tests/models/ Models: media, playlists, comments, subtitles tests/pipeline/ Upload, encoding, tasks, trim, and commands tests/rbac/ RBAC access tests/saml/, tests/lti/ SAML and LTI integrations tests/admin/, tests/pages/, tests/forms/ Admin portal, pages, forms tests/users/, tests/notifications/ Users and notifications tests/management/, tests/upgrade/ Management commands and site upgrade

Some tests carry the marker slow. Skip them with -m "not slow".

docs.title: Frontend tests
docs.text:
Frontend tests use Jest with the jsdom environment. The files are in frontend/tests/. The settings are in frontend/jest.config.js.

make test-frontend

This runs:

docker compose -f docker-compose-dev.yaml exec -T frontend npm run test -- --ci

Run with coverage:

make test-frontend-coverage

Run one test file:

docker compose -f docker-compose-dev.yaml exec -T frontend npm run test -- --ci tests/utils/settings/member.test.ts

docs.title: Check the result
docs.text:
1. Read the last line of the pytest output. It must show passed and no failed.
  2. Read the Jest summary. It must show Tests: with no failures.
  3. Run pre-commit run --all before you commit.

docs.title: Add a test
docs.text:
1. Put the file in the folder that matches the code. Name it test_<topic>.py.
  2. Do not call an outside host.
  3. Do not start real Celery workers. Eager mode runs the tasks.
  4. Run the new test alone, then run make test.

docs.title: Translations
docs.text:
Use this guide to add a text that users read in the interface, and to translate it. Follow the steps in order.

Warning

A pull request is not accepted if it skips these steps. Add the English text to files/frontend_translations/en.py first.

docs.title: MediaCMS Architecture
docs.text:
Translation files are Python modules in files/frontend_translations/. Django reads them. Django templates use them in two ways. React pages get them from the window.TRANSLATION object.

flowchart LR
    en["files/frontend_translations/en.py"] -->|"process_translations"| langs["fr.py, de.py, es.py, and other language files"]
    langs --> ctx["files/context_processors.py: get_translation"]
    ctx --> tpl["templates/config/installation/translations.html"]
    tpl --> win["window.TRANSLATION in the browser"]
    win --> react["React: translateString"]
    langs --> filter["Django templates: custom_translate filter"]
    react --> screen["Text on the screen"]
    filter --> screen

For the full stack, see Architecture.

docs.title: Files
docs.text:
File Purpose files/frontend_translations/en.py Source of every text. It has translation_strings and replacement_strings. files/frontend_translations/<lang>.py One file for each language. Language codes with a hyphen use an underscore: zh_hans.py, zh_hant.py. files/management/commands/process_translations.py Copies missing keys from en.py into all other files and sorts them.

translation_strings holds texts. replacement_strings holds small words that are replaced inside a longer text, for example month names and days ago.

docs.title: Add a text
docs.text:
1. Mark the text as translatable in the code.

    • In a React file, call translateString:

      import { translateString } from '../../utils/helpers/';

const label = translateString('Upload media');

    • In a Django template, use the custom_translate filter. See templates/cms/about.html for an example:

      {{ "About" | custom_translate:LANGUAGE_CODE }}

  2. Open files/frontend_translations/en.py.

  3. Add the text as a key in translation_strings. Use the exact English text as the key. Set the value to the same English text, or to an empty string.

    translation_strings = {
    # ...
    "My new label": "My new label",
}

  4. Run the command that copies the new key to all language files:

    docker compose -f docker-compose-dev.yaml exec -T web python manage.py process_translations

  5. Check the output. It must end with Successfully processed translation files.

  6. Open the file of your language, for example files/frontend_translations/fr.py.
  7. Find the key. Replace the English value with your translation.
  8. Commit en.py and every language file that changed.

Note

The command copies the English value into each language file. The site loads only non-empty values. An empty value means "not translated". The page then shows the English key.

docs.title: Translate an existing text
docs.text:
1. Open files/frontend_translations/<lang>.py.
  2. Find the key.
  3. Set the value to the translation.
  4. Keep placeholders such as {extra} and {link} unchanged.

docs.title: See the change
docs.text:
Where you added the text What you must do Django template Reload the page. The template does not need a frontend rebuild. React file Rebuild the frontend with make build-frontend. Python file only (en.py or a language file) Wait for Django to reload. If it does not, restart web: docker compose -f docker-compose-dev.yaml restart web.

Note

The webpack dev server on port 8088 shows React changes at once. Port 80 shows them only after make build-frontend. See Local development.

docs.title: Rules for texts
docs.text:
• Use one key for one text. Do not build a sentence from parts.
  • Keep the key short and clear.
  • Do not change a key that already exists. The change breaks all existing translations of it.
  • Keep UI labels the same as on the screen.

docs.title: Documentation translations
docs.text: Documentation pages are not part of this workflow. To add a language to the documentation site, see Add a documentation page.

docs.title: Operator guides
docs.text:
Use these guides when you are a portal editor or a portal manager. You run the library and the people of the portal. You do not change server settings.

Task Guide Needs Find, filter, and delete media and comments Manage media and comments Editor Decide what appears in public listings Review and publish Editor Organize media with categories and tags Categories and tags Editor to assign, manager to edit a category Understand who can see and edit media Permissions and RBAC Editor Add users, approve users, and give roles Manage users Manager

docs.title: MediaCMS Architecture
docs.text:
Operators work on the Manage pages. These pages read and change the same media and user records that the public pages use. Operators do not use the admin portal.

flowchart LR
    E[Editor] --> MM[Manage media]
    E --> MC[Manage comments]
    M[Manager] --> MU[Manage users]
    M --> MM
    M --> MC
    MM --> DB[(Media records)]
    MC --> DB2[(Comment records)]
    MU --> DB3[(User records)]
    DB --> L{Listable?}
    L -->|public + encoded + reviewed| PUB[Public listings]

Two checks decide what you can open:

  • is_mediacms_editor is true for editors, managers, and superusers. It opens Manage media and Manage comments.
  • is_mediacms_manager is true for managers and superusers. It opens Manage users and the manager actions.

A manager can do everything that an editor can do.

Note

The editor and manager roles are not the same as the RBAC roles (member, contributor, manager of a category group). Portal roles apply to the whole portal. RBAC roles apply to the categories of one group. See Permissions and RBAC.

docs.title: Check your role
docs.text:
1. Sign in.
  2. Open the menu on the left side of the page.
  3. Look for Manage media, Manage comments, and Manage users.

You see Manage users only when you are a manager or a superuser. If you see no Manage links, you are not an editor.

Warning

The admin portal at /admin/ is a separate surface for staff and superusers. A manager is not staff by default and cannot open it. See the Admin guides.

docs.title: Categories and tags
docs.text: Use this guide to organize media with categories and tags, and to edit a category.

docs.title: MediaCMS Architecture
docs.text:
A category and a tag are labels on media. They are stored once and linked to many media items. A category can also be an RBAC category, which controls access.

flowchart LR
    MD[Media item] --> CT[Categories]
    MD --> TG[Tags]
    CT --> G{RBAC category?}
    G -->|No| P[Label only]
    G -->|Yes| R[Access by RBAC group role]
    CT --> ED{can_edit_category?}
    ED -->|Portal manager| OK[Edit title, description, thumbnail]
    ED -->|Manager of this RBAC category| OK
    ED -->|Editor or other user| NO[Cannot edit the category]
Label Who creates it How it is used Category An administrator, in the admin portal A fixed group of media. One media item can be in many categories. Tag Any user who can edit the media A free keyword. A user enters a new keyword and it is created.

docs.title: Put media in a category
docs.text:
1. Open the media page.
  2. Select EDIT, then open the Publish tab.
  3. Select Category. Choose one or more categories.
  4. Select Publish Media.

An editor or a manager can choose any category. A user who is not an editor can choose only categories that are not RBAC categories, and the RBAC categories where that user is a contributor or manager. This applies when the portal uses RBAC.

Note

Adding media to an RBAC category gives the members of that group access to the media. Clear Shared and the RBAC categories are removed from the media. See Permissions and RBAC.

docs.title: Change categories or tags for many of your own media items
docs.text:
Bulk Actions work only on media that you own.

  1. Select My media in the menu.
  2. Select the check boxes of the media items.
  3. Select Bulk Actions.
  4. Select Add / Remove from Categories, or select Add / Remove Tags.
  5. Choose the labels and confirm.

docs.title: Tag media
docs.text:
1. Open the media page.
  2. Select EDIT, then open the Metadata tab.
  3. Enter Tags as a comma separated list.
  4. Select Update Media.

docs.title: Edit a category
docs.text:
You can edit a category when can_edit_category is true for you. This is true when:

  • You are a portal manager or a superuser. You can edit any category.
  • You are a manager of the RBAC group of an RBAC category. You can edit only that category.

An editor cannot edit a category. A contributor of an RBAC group can put media in the category but cannot rename it.

  1. Select Categories in the menu.
  2. Select the category.
  3. Select EDIT. If you do not see EDIT, you cannot edit this category.
  4. Change Title, Description, or Thumbnail. The thumbnail file must be 5 MB or smaller.
  5. Select Update category.

Note

The link to a category does not change when you change the title. The link uses an identifier that stays fixed.

docs.title: Create, delete, or make RBAC categories
docs.text: You cannot do these tasks on the Manage pages. A staff user or a superuser does them in the admin portal. See the Admin guides.

docs.title: Manage media and comments
docs.text: Use this guide to find media, check its status, and remove media or comments. You need the editor role to open Manage media and Manage comments.

docs.title: MediaCMS Architecture
docs.text:
The Manage pages read every media item and every comment. They do not apply the listing rule. You see media that is private, unlisted, not reviewed, and not encoded.

flowchart LR
    E[Editor or manager] --> P["/manage/media and /manage/comments"]
    P --> A["Manage API: /api/v1/manage_media, manage_comments"]
    A --> C{is_mediacms_editor?}
    C -->|No| R[Redirect or 403]
    C -->|Yes| D[(All media and comments)]
    D --> T[Table with filters and sort]
    T --> X{Delete media?}
    X -->|is_mediacms_manager| OK[Deleted]
    X -->|Editor only| NO[403 bad permissions]
  • is_mediacms_editor opens both pages. It is true for editors, managers, and superusers.
  • Deleting media from the Manage pages needs is_mediacms_manager. Deleting a comment needs only the editor role.

docs.title: Open the Manage pages
docs.text:
1. Sign in as an editor or a manager.
  2. Open the menu on the left side of the page.
  3. Select Manage media or Manage comments.

If you do not see these links, your account is not an editor. Ask a manager. See Manage users.

docs.title: Find media
docs.text:
1. Open Manage media.
  2. Enter a title in the search field. To search by owner, change the field to Owner and enter a name or a user name.
  3. Select Filters to narrow the list.
  4. Select a column heading, such as Title or the date, to sort.

The filters are:

Filter Values STATE All, Public, Private, Unlisted MEDIA TYPE All, Video, Audio, Image, Pdf ENCODING STATUS All, Success, Running, Pending, Fail REVIEWED All, Yes, No FEATURED All, Yes, No CATEGORY All, or one category

Each row shows Author, Media type, Encoding status, State, Reviewed, Featured, and Reported.

docs.title: Common searches
docs.text: You want to find Set Media that waits for review REVIEWED: No Media that failed to encode ENCODING STATUS: Fail Media that is still processing ENCODING STATUS: Running or Pending Media that is not listable although it is reviewed STATE: not Public, or ENCODING STATUS: not Success

docs.title: Change media
docs.text:
1. Select the title of a media item. The media page opens.
  2. Select EDIT.
  3. Change the metadata, or open the Publish tab to change the state, Featured, or Is reviewed.

See Review and publish.

docs.title: Delete media
docs.text:
1. Open Manage media.
  2. Select Delete in the row of the item. Or select the check boxes of several items, select Bulk actions, select Delete selected, and select Apply.
  3. Select PROCEED.

Warning

Deleting media removes the media record and its files. You cannot undo it.

Note

Only managers can delete media on the Manage pages. If an editor selects Delete, the portal answers "bad permissions". A bulk delete handles up to 50 items for each request.

An editor can still delete a media item from its own media page. Select More options, then Delete.

docs.title: Moderate comments
docs.text:
1. Open Manage comments.
  2. Select View media in a row to read the comment in context.
  3. Select Delete in the row to remove a comment. Or select several rows, select Bulk actions, select Delete selected, and select Apply.
  4. Select PROCEED.

The list shows the newest comments first. Select a column heading to sort.

Note

To turn comments off for one media item, clear Enable comments on its Metadata tab.

docs.title: Manage users
docs.text: Use this guide to create users, approve users, and give roles. You need the manager role (is_mediacms_manager). Editors cannot open Manage users.

docs.title: MediaCMS Architecture
docs.text:
User management crosses two screens and one API. The Manage users page lists, creates, approves, and deletes users. The user edit form gives roles.

flowchart LR
    M[Manager] --> MU["Manage users: /manage/users"]
    MU --> API["/api/v1/users and /api/v1/users/username"]
    API --> C{is_mediacms_manager?}
    C -->|No| X[Refused]
    C -->|Yes| A{Target is a superuser?}
    A -->|Yes, and you are not a superuser| Y[Password change and delete refused]
    A -->|No| U[(User record)]
    M --> EF["User edit form: /user/username/edit"]
    EF --> R[Roles: advanced user, Editor, Manager]
    R --> U
    U --> AP{Is approved?}
    AP -->|Needed and false| P[Pending: can browse only]
    AP -->|Yes| F[Full access for the role]
  • A manager opens Manage users, creates users, approves users, gives the roles Editor and Manager, changes passwords, and deletes users.
  • A manager is not staff by default. A manager cannot open the admin portal at /admin/.
  • A manager cannot change the password of a superuser. A manager cannot delete a superuser. The portal refuses both actions.
  • The user edit form has no field to make a user a superuser or to make a user staff. Those flags are set in the admin portal, which a manager cannot open.

Note

The portal checks the manager role again on the server for every action. Hiding a button in the interface is not the only guard.

docs.title: Open Manage users
docs.text:
1. Sign in as a manager.
  2. Open the menu on the left side of the page.
  3. Select Manage users.

If you do not see Manage users, your account is not a manager. A superuser or another manager must give you the role.

docs.title: Find a user
docs.text:
1. Open Manage users.
  2. Enter a name or a user name in the search field. When the portal owner allows it, you can also search by email.
  3. Select Filters.
  4. Under ROLE, select All, Editor, or Manager.
  5. When the portal needs approval, select Yes or No under APPROVED to find users that wait for approval.

Each row shows the name, user name, date added, role, and approval state.

docs.title: Create a user
docs.text:
1. Open Manage users.
  2. Select Add New User.
  3. Enter Username, Password, Email, and Name. All four fields are required.
  4. Select SUBMIT.

The portal refuses the request when the user name or the email is already in use.

Note

A new user has no role and is not approved. When the portal needs approval, approve the user before the user signs in.

docs.title: Approve a user
docs.text:
Use this when the portal owner turned on USERS_NEEDS_TO_BE_APPROVED. An unapproved user can sign in and browse. The user cannot upload or change media. A pending user sees the page Account Pending Approval.

  1. Open Manage users.
  2. Under APPROVED, select No to list the users that wait.
  3. Find the user. Select Approve in the row.
  4. Select PROCEED.

The row now shows the approved mark.

docs.title: Assign a role
docs.text:
Roles are check boxes on the user edit form.

  1. Open Manage users.
  2. Select the name of the user. The profile page opens.
  3. Select the edit icon (Edit profile).
  4. Select the roles you want:
    • MediaCMS Editor lets the user open Manage media and Manage comments.
    • MediaCMS Manager lets the user also manage users.
    • advanced user marks the user for features that the portal owner limits to advanced users.
  5. Select Is approved if the portal needs approval and the user is ready.
  6. Select Update Profile.

Give the lowest role that does the job. An editor does not need the manager role.

Warning

A MediaCMS Manager can create users, give roles, and delete users and media. Give this role to few people.

docs.title: Change a password
docs.text:
1. Open Manage users.
  2. Select Change password in the row of the user.
  3. Enter New Password.
  4. Select SUBMIT.

The portal checks the password rules. If you try this on a superuser, the portal answers that you do not have permission.

docs.title: Delete users
docs.text:
1. Open Manage users.
  2. Select Delete in the row. Or select the check boxes of several users, select Bulk actions, select Delete selected, and select Apply.
  3. Select PROCEED.

Warning

Deleting a user also deletes the media of that user. You cannot undo it. The portal refuses to delete a superuser.

docs.title: What a manager cannot do
docs.text:
Task Who can do it Open the admin portal (/admin/) Staff and superusers Make a user a superuser or staff People who have access to the admin portal Change the password of a superuser A superuser Delete a superuser A superuser Create RBAC groups and memberships Staff and superusers, in the admin portal

See the Manager role and the Admin guides.

docs.title: Permissions and RBAC
docs.text: Use this guide to understand who can see and edit a media item. Read it before you share media or change roles.

docs.title: MediaCMS Architecture
docs.text:
Four layers decide access. The server checks them in this order for a private media item.

flowchart TD
    R[Request to open media] --> S{Media state}
    S -->|Public or Unlisted| OK[Allowed]
    S -->|Private| O{Is the user the owner?}
    O -->|Yes| OK
    O -->|No| E{Portal editor, manager, or superuser?}
    E -->|Yes| OK
    E -->|No| MP{MediaPermission on this media?}
    MP -->|Yes| OK
    MP -->|No| RB{USE_RBAC and member of a group<br/>that has a category of this media?}
    RB -->|Yes| OK
    RB -->|No| NO[Refused]

docs.title: Layer 1: Media state
docs.text:
Each media item has one state.

State In listings Opens for Public Yes, when the media is listable Everyone Unlisted No Anyone who has the link Private No The owner, people with access, editors

Listable media is public, encoded, and reviewed. See Review and publish.

docs.title: Layer 2: MediaPermission (direct share)
docs.text:
A MediaPermission gives one user access to one media item. The owner of the media or a user with the owner permission creates it.

Permission Can open Can edit metadata Can delete or share further Viewer Yes No No Editor Yes Yes No Owner Yes Yes Yes

In the interface these are Co-Viewer, Co-Editor, and Co-Owner. See Share and embed.

docs.title: Layer 3: RBAC (category groups)
docs.text:
When the portal owner sets USE_RBAC, a category can be an RBAC category. An RBAC group holds users and links to RBAC categories. Each user has one role in the group.

RBAC role In the RBAC category Member Can see the media. Contributor Can see and edit the media, and can add media to the category. Manager Full control of the media. Can also edit the category.

A media item gets RBAC access through its categories. A user who belongs to a group with that category gets the access of the role.

Note

A staff user or a superuser creates RBAC groups and memberships in the admin portal. Single sign-on can also assign groups. See the Admin guides.

docs.title: Layer 4: Portal roles
docs.text:
Portal roles apply to the whole portal. They are separate from RBAC roles.

Portal role Check Powers Editor (MediaCMS Editor) is_mediacms_editor Opens Manage media and Manage comments. Opens every media item. Sets any state. Changes Is reviewed, Featured, and Reported times. Uploads without the usual limits. Manager (MediaCMS Manager) is_mediacms_manager All editor powers. Opens Manage users. Creates, approves, and deletes users. Deletes media on the Manage pages. Edits any category. Superuser is_superuser Everything. Counts as manager and editor.

is_mediacms_editor is true for editors, managers, and superusers. is_mediacms_manager is true for managers and superusers.

Warning

Do not confuse the two kinds of roles. A manager of an RBAC group has power only in the categories of that group. A MediaCMS Manager has power over the whole portal. The names are the same. The powers are not.

Question Portal role RBAC role Where is it set? The user edit form, by a manager The admin portal, or single sign-on What does it cover? The whole portal The categories of one group Can it open Manage media? Yes, for editor or higher No Can it edit a category? Manager, yes. Editor, no. Manager of that category, yes

docs.title: Related user flags
docs.text:
• advanced user is a flag that the portal owner can use to decide who can upload or comment. It is not an editor power.
  • Is approved applies when the portal needs approval for new users. A user who is not approved can browse but cannot upload or change anything. See Manage users.

docs.title: Check access for a media item
docs.text:
1. Open Manage media and find the media.
  2. Open the media page.
  3. Select More options, then Status info, to read the state.
  4. Check the categories on the Publish tab.
  5. Check Shared by me on the profile of the owner for direct shares.

docs.title: Review and publish
docs.text: Use this guide to control what appears in public listings. You need the editor role to mark media as reviewed.

docs.title: MediaCMS Architecture
docs.text:
A media item appears in public listings only when it is listable. The server recomputes this value each time the media is saved.

flowchart LR
    UP[Upload] --> ST[State from PORTAL_WORKFLOW]
    UP --> RV[is_reviewed from MEDIA_IS_REVIEWED]
    UP --> EN[Encoding]
    EN --> ES[encoding_status]
    ST --> L{state = public<br/>AND encoding_status = success<br/>AND is_reviewed}
    RV --> L
    ES --> L
    L -->|All true| Y[listable = true: public listings]
    L -->|Any false| N[listable = false: hidden from listings]
    ED[Editor: Publish tab] -->|Change state or Is reviewed| ST
    ED --> RV

Listable rule: media is listable when the state is public AND the encoding status is success AND the media is reviewed. If one condition is false, the media is not listable.

Media that is not listable still opens for the owner, for people with direct access, for RBAC members, and for editors. It does not appear in public listings.

docs.title: Settings that set the starting values
docs.text:
The portal owner sets these in cms/local_settings.py. A change needs a restart.

Setting Values Effect on new media PORTAL_WORKFLOW public State starts as public. unlisted State starts as unlisted. private State starts as private. private_verified State starts as unlisted for advanced users and private for other users. MEDIA_IS_REVIEWED True (default) New media is reviewed at once. False New media is not reviewed. An editor must review it.

Note

These settings set only the starting values of new media. A change does not alter media that exists.

Examples:

  • With PORTAL_WORKFLOW = "public" and MEDIA_IS_REVIEWED = True, new media becomes listable when encoding succeeds.
  • With MEDIA_IS_REVIEWED = False, new media waits for you. It does not become listable until you mark it as reviewed.
  • With PORTAL_WORKFLOW = "private", new media is private. An editor must set it to public.

Users who are not editors have limits on the state. When the workflow is not public, a user can pick only Private or Unlisted. An editor can set any state.

docs.title: Find media that needs review
docs.text:
1. Open Manage media.
  2. Select Filters.
  3. Under REVIEWED, select No.

Add ENCODING STATUS: Success to see only media that is ready.

docs.title: Mark media as reviewed
docs.text:
1. Open the media page.
  2. Select EDIT.
  3. Open the Publish tab.
  4. Select Is reviewed.
  5. Check State. For public listings, select Public.
  6. Select Publish Media.

To remove media from public listings, clear Is reviewed, or change the state. Then select Publish Media.

Note

Only editors and managers can change Is reviewed, Featured, and Reported times. For other users these fields are read-only.

docs.title: Check why media is not listable
docs.text:
1. Open the media page.
  2. Select More options, then Status info.
  3. Read each line.

Note

Status info appears for video only. For other media types, read the columns Encoding status, State, and Reviewed on Manage media. Image, PDF, and audio items have the encoding status success at once.

Line What you need State public Encoding Status success Review state Is reviewed Result Action State is not public Set Public on the Publish tab. Review state is Pending review Select Is reviewed on the Publish tab. Encoding Status is pending or running Wait. The worker is still encoding. Encoding Status is fail Ask an administrator to check the processing queue.

Warning

Reported media can become private automatically. The portal sets the media to private when the number of reports reaches the limit that the portal owner set (REPORTED_TIMES_THRESHOLD, 10 by default). Check the Reported column on Manage media.

docs.title: User guides
docs.text:
Use these guides to watch, upload, and share media in MediaCMS. You do not need special powers for most tasks.

Task Guide Find and play media Browse and play Find media by text, type, or date Search Add a video, audio, image, or PDF file Upload Change title, description, tags, and state Edit your media Add subtitles to a video Captions Add comments, mentions, and timestamps Comments and mentions Group media in a list Playlists Send a link or embed media Share and embed Cut a video Trim Change your picture and details Profile Save a copy of media Download

docs.title: MediaCMS Architecture
docs.text:
You use the public pages of MediaCMS. These pages read media records from the database. They play files that the server stores.

flowchart LR
    V[You] --> W[Pages: browse, search, media, profile]
    W --> L{Is the media listable?}
    L -->|Yes| S[Shown in listings]
    L -->|No| X[Hidden from listings]
    X --> Y[Open by link or by access you have]

Media is listable when all three conditions are true:

  • The media state is public.
  • Encoding succeeded.
  • The media is reviewed. On many portals new media is reviewed at upload. On other portals an editor must mark it as reviewed first.

Media that is not listable does not appear in public listings. You can still open your own media. You can also open media that other people shared with you.

Note

The portal owner sets some rules. For example, the portal owner decides who can upload, who can comment, and whether new media is public. If a control is missing, ask the portal owner.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Sign in to upload, comment, make playlists, or edit a profile. You can browse without an account when the portal allows it.
  • If your account needs approval, you can browse but you cannot change anything. A manager must approve your account first.

docs.title: Browse and play
docs.text: Use this guide to find media in the lists and to play it.

docs.title: MediaCMS Architecture
docs.text:
Each list page asks the server for media. The server returns only the media that you may see.

flowchart LR
    B[List page] --> Q[Media query]
    Q --> A[Listable media]
    Q --> S[Media shared with you]
    Q --> R[Media in RBAC categories you belong to]
    A --> O[Result list]
    S --> O
    R --> O
  • Listable media is public, encoded, and reviewed.
  • Shared media is media where another user gave you access.
  • RBAC media appears only when the portal uses RBAC and you belong to a matching category group.

docs.title: Browse the lists
docs.text:
1. Open the portal home page.
  2. Open the menu on the left side of the page.
  3. Select a list: Home, Featured, Recommended, Latest, Categories, Tags, Members, History, or Liked media.
  4. Select a media item to open its page.

Note

You see My media and My playlists only after you sign in. You see Members only when the portal owner allows it.

docs.title: Browse by category or tag
docs.text:
1. Select Categories in the menu.
  2. Select a category. The page lists the media in that category.
  3. Select Tags to browse by tag in the same way.

docs.title: Play media
docs.text:
1. Open a media page.
  2. Select the play button on the player.
  3. Use the player controls to pause, change the volume, change the video quality, or go to full screen.
  4. Turn on AUTOPLAY to play the next related item when the current item ends.

docs.title: Act on media
docs.text:
Under the player you can select:

  • LIKE or the dislike icon, to rate the media.
  • SHARE, to send a link. See Share and embed.
  • SAVE, to add the media to a playlist. See Playlists.
  • DOWNLOAD, when the owner allows it. See Download.
  • More options, then Report, to report media that breaks the rules.

Note

The portal owner can turn each of these controls on or off. Some actions need you to sign in.

docs.title: Media that does not play yet
docs.text: A video can show a message that encoding has not started or is still running. The page then tries to play the original video file. Playback can be slow or can fail. Wait until encoding finishes, then open the page again. See Upload.

docs.title: Captions
docs.text: Use this guide to add, edit, and delete captions (subtitles) for a video or audio item.

docs.title: MediaCMS Architecture
docs.text:
Captions are separate files that belong to one media item. The player loads them next to the video. A caption file does not change the video or its encodes.

flowchart LR
    U[You: Captions tab] --> F[SRT or VTT file]
    F --> S[(Subtitle record for the media)]
    W[Optional: automatic transcription] --> Q[Celery worker with Whisper]
    Q --> S
    S --> P[Video player: CC button]
  • You upload a SubRip (.srt) file or a WebVTT (.vtt) file. You choose one language for each file.
  • Automatic transcription works only when the portal owner turns on Whisper. The portal then shows an extra section on the Captions tab.

docs.title: Add a caption file
docs.text:
1. Open the media page.
  2. Select EDIT, then select the Captions tab.
  3. Under Upload Caption File, select the file.
  4. Select the Language of the file.
  5. Select Submit.

The new language appears in the list Edit existing Captions.

docs.title: Request automatic transcription
docs.text:
1. Open the Captions tab.
  2. Find the section Request Automatic Transcription and Translation. If you do not see it, the portal does not offer it to you.
  3. Select Transcription. Select English Translation if you also need an English version.
  4. Select Submit in that section.

Note

You cannot clear Transcription or English Translation after the server accepts the request. The worker needs time to finish the job.

docs.title: Edit a caption file
docs.text:
1. Open the Captions tab.
  2. Under Edit existing Captions, select a language.
  3. Change the text in the editor.
  4. Select SAVE.

Select DOWNLOAD to save the caption file to your computer.

docs.title: Delete a caption file
docs.text:
1. Open the Captions tab.
  2. Select the language under Edit existing Captions.
  3. Select DELETE.
  4. Select DELETE SUBTITLE to confirm.

docs.title: Show captions in the player
docs.text:
1. Play the video.
  2. Select the CC button on the player.
  3. Select a language, or select the off option.

docs.title: Comments and mentions
docs.text: Use this guide to add comments, mention other users, and link to a time in a video.

docs.title: MediaCMS Architecture
docs.text:
A comment is a text record that belongs to one media item and one user. The server reads the text when you post it. It finds mentions and timestamps and turns them into links.

flowchart LR
    A[You write a comment] --> B[Comment API]
    B --> C[(Comment record)]
    B --> D{Text has a mention?}
    D -->|Yes| E[Link to user page and optional email]
    B --> F{Text has a timestamp?}
    F -->|Yes| G[Timestamp link in the comment]
    G --> H[Timebar dot, when turned on]
    C --> I[Media owner is notified]

docs.title: Add a comment
docs.text:
1. Sign in.
  2. Open a media page.
  3. Select the field Add a comment....
  4. Enter your text.
  5. Select SUBMIT.

Use Newest first or Oldest first to change the order of the list.

Note

You cannot comment when you see Comments are disabled. The media owner turned comments off, or the portal owner limits who can comment.

docs.title: Mention a user
docs.text:
When the portal owner turns on mentions, you can mention other users.

  1. Type @ in the comment field. A list of user names opens.
  2. Continue to type to narrow the list.
  3. Select a user from the list.
  4. Select SUBMIT.

The comment shows a link to the page of that user. The portal can also send an email to the user.

Note

A mention is one block. If you edit the mention text, the field removes the whole mention. Select the user again.

docs.title: Link to a time in the video
docs.text:
1. Write a time in your comment. Use the format MM:SS or HH:MM:SS. For example, 02:15.
  2. Select SUBMIT.

The server turns the time into a link. When a viewer selects the link, the player jumps to that time.

docs.title: Show comments in the timebar
docs.text:
When the portal owner turns on this feature, a comment that contains a valid timestamp also shows as a colored dot on the timebar of the video.

  1. Play a video that has timestamped comments.
  2. Move the pointer over a dot to preview the comment.
  3. Play to the time of the dot. The comment shows on top of the video.

Only the formats MM:SS and HH:MM:SS create a dot.

docs.title: Link to a time without a comment
docs.text:
1. Pause the video at the time that you want.
  2. Select SHARE.
  3. Select the Start at check box.
  4. Copy the link.

See Share and embed.

docs.title: Delete a comment
docs.text:
You can delete a comment when one of these is true:

  • You wrote the comment.
  • You own the media.

  • You are a portal editor, manager, or superuser.

  • Find the comment.

  • Select DELETE COMMENT.
  • Confirm.

Editors can also delete many comments at once. See Manage media and comments.

docs.title: Download
docs.text: Use this guide to save a copy of media, and to turn downloads on or off for your own media.

docs.title: MediaCMS Architecture
docs.text:
The download control reads two things: the Allow download setting of the media, and the files that the server stores. A video has one file for each encode and the original file.

flowchart LR
    V[Viewer] --> B{Allow download on?}
    B -->|No| X[No DOWNLOAD control]
    B -->|Yes| D[DOWNLOAD control]
    D --> F[(Stored files)]
    F --> E[Encoded files by resolution]
    F --> O[Original file, if the portal allows it]

docs.title: Download media
docs.text:
1. Open the media page.
  2. Select DOWNLOAD under the player. On a small screen, select More options, then Download.
  3. For a video, choose a version. Choose an encoded file, or choose Original file.
  4. Save the file when your browser asks.

For an image, audio, or PDF item, DOWNLOAD saves the file at once.

Note

You do not see DOWNLOAD when the owner turned downloads off or when the portal owner turned off the control. The portal owner can also hide the original file.

docs.title: Turn downloads on or off for your media
docs.text:
1. Open the media page.
  2. Select EDIT, then open the Publish tab.
  3. Select Allow download to turn downloads on. Clear it to turn them off.
  4. Select Publish Media.

Downloads are on by default.

docs.title: Turn downloads on or off for many items
docs.text:
1. Select My media in the menu.
  2. Select the check boxes of the media items.
  3. Select Bulk Actions, then Settings, then Enable Download or Disable Download.
  4. Confirm.

docs.title: Edit your media
docs.text: Use this guide to change the title, tags, description, state, and other settings of media that you own.

docs.title: MediaCMS Architecture
docs.text:
The edit page has tabs. Each tab changes a different part of the media record. The Publish tab changes who can see the media.

flowchart LR
    M[Media page: EDIT] --> T[Edit tabs]
    T --> Meta[Metadata: title, tags, description, poster]
    T --> Pub[Publish: category, state, download]
    T --> Other[Trim, Captions, Chapters]
    Meta --> R[(Media record)]
    Pub --> R
    R --> Q{State public, encoded, reviewed?}
    Q -->|Yes| L[Listable]
    Q -->|No| H[Not in public listings]

You can edit media when you are the owner. You can also edit media when an owner gave you the editor permission, when you are a contributor in a matching RBAC category, or when you are a portal editor or manager.

docs.title: Open the edit page
docs.text:
1. Open the media page.
  2. Select EDIT.
  3. Select a tab: Metadata, Trim, Captions, Chapters, Publish, or Replace.

Note

Trim, Captions, and Chapters appear for video and audio only. Replace appears only when the portal owner turns it on.

docs.title: Change the metadata
docs.text:
1. Open the Metadata tab.
  2. Change Title.
  3. Enter Tags as a comma separated list.
  4. Enter the Description.
  5. Clear Enable comments to turn comments off for this media.
  6. For a video, enter Thumbnail Time (seconds) to choose the thumbnail frame.
  7. For video and audio, select a file for Poster Image to use your own image. The file must be 5 MB or smaller.
  8. Select Update Media.

Note

The Slug field appears only when the portal owner allows custom media URLs. The slug can contain letters, numbers, hyphens, and underscores.

docs.title: Change the state and the category
docs.text:
1. Open the Publish tab.
  2. Select Category and choose one or more categories.
  3. Under State, select Private, Unlisted, or Public.
  4. Select or clear Allow download.
  5. Select Publish Media.
State Who can find the media Who can open it Public Everyone, in listings, when the media is listable Everyone Unlisted Nobody in listings Anyone who has the link Private Nobody in listings You and people you gave access to

Note

The portal owner can limit the states that you can pick. When the portal workflow is not public, you can pick only Private and Unlisted. An editor can pick Public for you.

The fields Featured, Reported times, and Is reviewed are read-only for you. Only editors and managers can change them. See Review and publish.

docs.title: Add captions, trim, or replace
docs.text:
• Select Captions to add subtitles. See Captions.
  • Select Trim to cut the video. See Trim.
  • Select Replace to upload a new file for the same media.

docs.title: Delete media
docs.text:
1. Open the media page.
  2. Select More options, then Delete.
  3. Confirm.

Warning

Delete removes the media and its files. You cannot undo it.

docs.title: Playlists
docs.text: Use this guide to group media in an ordered list and to play the list.

docs.title: MediaCMS Architecture
docs.text:
A playlist is a list that belongs to one user. It holds links to media. It does not copy the media files.

flowchart LR
    M[Media page: SAVE] --> P[Playlist selector]
    P --> L[(Playlist record)]
    L --> I[Ordered links to media]
    I --> V[Playlist page and playback]
    V --> A{Can you open each media item?}
    A -->|Yes| S[Item plays]
    A -->|No| H[Item is hidden from the list]

The playlist page hides items that the viewer cannot open. Adding a private item to a playlist does not make the item public.

docs.title: Create a playlist and add media
docs.text:
1. Sign in.
  2. Open a media page.
  3. Select SAVE.
  4. Select Create a new playlist.
  5. Enter the playlist title. Enter a description if you want.
  6. Select CREATE.

The media is now in the playlist.

docs.title: Add media to an existing playlist
docs.text:
1. Open a media page.
  2. Select SAVE. The window Save to... opens.
  3. Select the check box of the playlist.

Clear the check box to remove the media from the playlist.

docs.title: Find your playlists
docs.text:
1. Select My playlists in the menu.
  2. Select a playlist to open it.

You can also open your profile and select Playlists.

docs.title: Play a playlist
docs.text:
1. Open a playlist.
  2. Select a media item. The player plays the items in order.

docs.title: Edit a playlist
docs.text:
1. Open the playlist. You must be the owner.
  2. Select EDIT. The window Edit playlist opens.
  3. Change the title or the description.
  4. Select UPDATE.

Note

The portal owner sets the maximum number of media items in one playlist. If you cannot add more items, the playlist is full.

docs.title: Delete a playlist
docs.text:
1. Open the playlist. You must be the owner.
  2. Open the playlist options and select Delete.
  3. Select PROCEED.

Warning

Deleting a playlist does not delete the media. It removes only the list.

docs.title: Profile
docs.text: Use this guide to change your profile, to find your media, and to delete your account.

docs.title: MediaCMS Architecture
docs.text:
Your profile is a user record with a page for each list: media, playlists, and about. Only you and managers can edit the profile.

flowchart LR
    U[You] --> P[Profile page]
    P --> T[Tabs: About, Media I own, Shared by me, Shared with me, Playlists]
    U --> E[Edit Profile form]
    E --> R[(User record)]
    R --> P

docs.title: Open your profile
docs.text:
1. Select your picture at the top of the page to open the user menu.
  2. Select the link to your profile.

docs.title: Edit your profile
docs.text:
1. Open your profile.
  2. Select the edit icon (Edit profile) on your profile page.
  3. Change full name, About me, or the logo.
  4. Select or clear the notification option. When it is selected, you receive an email when someone comments on your media.
  5. Select Update Profile.

Note

The logo file must be 2 MB or smaller. If you signed in through an identity provider, you cannot change your name here.

docs.title: Use the profile tabs
docs.text:
• About shows your description.
  • Media I own lists your media. You can filter it by sharing, tag, and sort order.
  • Shared by me lists media that you shared with other users.
  • Shared with me lists media that other users shared with you.
  • Playlists lists your playlists. See Playlists.

docs.title: Delete your account
docs.text:
1. Open Edit Profile.
  2. Go to Danger Zone.
  3. Select Delete Account.
  4. Confirm.

Warning

This removes all your data, including your media and playlists. You cannot undo it.

docs.title: Change your role or approval
docs.text: You cannot change your own role or approval. A manager does that. See Manage users.

docs.title: Search
docs.text: Use this guide to find media by text, type, or date.

docs.title: MediaCMS Architecture
docs.text:
The search field sends your text to the search service of MediaCMS. The service searches the media that you may see. It does not search private media that you cannot open.

flowchart LR
    F[Search field] --> R[Results page]
    R --> API[Search API]
    API --> V[Media you can see]
    V --> L[Sorted and filtered list]

docs.title: Search for media
docs.text:
1. Select the search field at the top of the page.
  2. Enter one or more words.
  3. Press Enter, or select the search icon.
  4. Select a result to open it.

While you type, the field can suggest matching titles. Select a suggestion to go to that media.

docs.title: Filter the results
docs.text:
1. On the results page, select Filters.
  2. Under MEDIA TYPE, select All, Video, Audio, Image, or Pdf.
  3. Under UPLOAD DATE, select All, Today, This week, This month, or This year.
  4. Under SORT BY, select Upload date (newest), Upload date (oldest), View count, or Like count.

The list updates when you select an option.

docs.title: Search inside a category, tag, or author
docs.text:
• Select a category in Categories to see only media in that category.
  • Select a tag in Tags to see only media with that tag.
  • Select an author name on a media page to see the media of that author.

Note

Search finds only media that you may see. If you cannot find a media item, the media can be private, not yet reviewed, or still encoding. See Upload.

docs.title: Share and embed
docs.text: Use this guide to send a link to media, to start the link at a time, to embed media in another page, and to share private media with named users.

docs.title: MediaCMS Architecture
docs.text:
A link does not give access by itself. The media state and the permissions on the media decide who can open it.

flowchart TD
    S[SHARE link or embed code] --> V[Viewer opens the link]
    V --> C{Media state}
    C -->|Public| A[Anyone can open it]
    C -->|Unlisted| B[Anyone with the link can open it]
    C -->|Private| D{Does the viewer have access?}
    D -->|Owner, MediaPermission, RBAC member, or editor| E[Opens]
    D -->|No| F[Refused]
  • Public and Unlisted media open for anyone who has the link. Public media also appears in listings when it is listable.
  • Private media opens only for the owner, for people with a direct share (MediaPermission), for members of a matching RBAC category, and for editors.

docs.title: Trim
docs.text: Use this guide to cut a video or audio file. You can replace the original, save the cut as new media, or make separate media from segments.

docs.title: MediaCMS Architecture
docs.text:
A trim is a request that a Celery worker runs in the background. The trim does not re-encode the file. The worker cuts the file at the times that you set.

flowchart LR
    U[You: Trim tab] --> R[Trim request]
    R --> W[Celery worker]
    W --> A{Action}
    A -->|Replace Original| O[Original file replaced]
    A -->|Save as New| N[New media item]
    A -->|Create Segments| S[One media item for each segment]
    O --> E[Encoding runs again]
    N --> E
    S --> E
    E --> L{Public, encoded, reviewed?}
    L -->|Yes| P[Listable]
  • Each new or changed file goes through encoding again. Until encoding succeeds, the media is not listable.
  • Only one trim request can run for a video at a time.

docs.title: Trim a video
docs.text:
1. Open the media page.
  2. Select EDIT, then select the Trim tab.
  3. Play the video. Use the timeline controls of the editor to choose the part to keep.
  4. Add more segments if you need them.
  5. Choose the action: Replace Original, Save as New, or Create Segments.
  6. Confirm the action.

The page shows a message that the video is processing. You see the result at once. The server finishes the work in the background.

Action Result Replace Original The cut replaces the original file of this media. Save as New The cut becomes a new media item. The original stays. Create Segments Each segment becomes a separate media item.

Warning

Replace Original changes the file of the media. You cannot go back to the earlier file.

Note

The Trim tab appears for video and audio only. The portal owner can turn trimming off. If the tab is missing or the page shows Video Trimmer is not enabled, ask the portal owner.

docs.title: Speed
docs.text:
• If encoding is finished for all resolutions, the trim runs fast.
  • If you upload a video and trim it at once, the trim starts the processing. It takes more time.

docs.title: Upload
docs.text: Use this guide to add a video, audio, image, or PDF file to MediaCMS.

docs.title: MediaCMS Architecture
docs.text:
An upload crosses three stages: the upload, encoding, and the listing. The media appears in public listings only after all three succeed.

flowchart LR
    U[You: Upload page] --> F[Original file stored on the server]
    F --> T{Media type}
    T -->|Image, PDF, or audio| OK[Encoding status: success]
    T -->|Video| E[Encoding queue]
    E --> C[Long video split into chunks]
    C --> P[One encode for each enabled profile]
    P --> J[Chunks joined into one file per resolution]
    J --> S[First MP4 or WebM encode succeeds]
    S --> OK
    J --> H[HLS version made]
    OK --> G{State public and reviewed?}
    G -->|Yes| L[Listable: shown in public listings]
    G -->|No| N[Not listed: owner and people with access can open it]
  • The server stores your original file first.
  • A Celery worker encodes video. It makes one encode for each enabled encode profile (for example, 240p, 480p, and 720p).
  • Image, PDF, and audio files do not need encoding. Their encoding status is success at once.
  • For video, the encoding status becomes success when at least one MP4 or WebM encode finishes. Other resolutions and the HLS version can finish later.
  • If the server cannot read the file, the encoding status is fail.
  • The media is listable when the state is public, the encoding status is success, and the media is reviewed.

docs.title: Upload a file
docs.text:
1. Sign in.
  2. Select Upload media at the top of the page.
  3. Select Browse your files, or drag a file into the drop area.
  4. Select the file in the file dialog.
  5. Wait for the progress bar to complete.
  6. Select View media to open the media page.

If you cannot select Upload media, the portal does not allow you to upload. Read the message on the page.

Note

You can select Pause and Continue to stop and restart a large upload. Select Cancel to stop an upload. Select Retry after an error.

docs.text:
1. Open the media page.
  2. Select EDIT.
  3. Enter the title, the description, and the tags.
  4. Select Update Media.

See Edit your media for all fields.

docs.title: What state does the media get?
docs.text:
The portal owner sets the state of new media. A new item can be public, unlisted, or private. Open the Publish tab on the edit page to see the state. Change it there if the portal allows you.

Warning

New media can be hidden from public listings for three reasons: the state is not public, encoding is not finished, or the media is not reviewed. You can open the media yourself. Other people cannot find it in listings.

docs.title: Check the encoding status
docs.text:
1. Open the media page.
  2. Select More options, then Status info.
  3. Read Encoding Status. The values are pending, running, success, and fail.

If the status is fail, ask an editor or an administrator to check the media.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• Allowed file types are set by the portal owner. The default types are video, audio, image, and PDF.
  • The portal owner sets the maximum file size and the number of files you can upload.
  • On some portals, only approved users, users with a verified email, or advanced users can upload.

docs.text: Reference for the MediaCMS frontend code in frontend/.

docs.title: The frontend is an application, not an HTTP API
docs.text:
The frontend is a set of React bundles. It does not serve HTTP requests and it has no routes of its own. Django owns the routes, the pages, the data, and the login. Each Django template loads one bundle. The bundle then calls the Django REST API.

For the HTTP API, read the REST API page. This page does not describe any HTTP endpoints.

docs.title: MediaCMS Architecture
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    entry["frontend/src/entries/name.js"] -->|"webpack build"| bundle["static/js/name.js"]
    commons["static/js/_commons.js"] --> page
    bundle --> page["Browser page"]
    tpl["templates/cms/page.html"] -->|"script tag"| bundle
    tpl --> commons
    view["Django view in files/views or users/views"] -->|"render"| tpl
    page -->|"fetch"| api["REST API: /api/v1/"]
    api --> db[("PostgreSQL")]

For the full stack, see Architecture. To run and build the frontend, see Local development.

docs.title: Entry points
docs.text:
webpack makes one bundle for each *.js file in frontend/src/entries/. The file name, without .js, is the bundle name. The build writes the bundle to static/js/<name>.js. The settings are in frontend/webpack.config.js.

  • A Django template loads static/js/<name>.js and static/js/_commons.js.
  • The shared code of all bundles is in _commons.js. The shared styles are in _commons.css.
  • Most entries call renderPage('page-<name>', <PageComponent>). The page component is in frontend/src/static/js/pages/.
  • The entry embed calls renderEmbedPage.
  • The entries add-media and base call renderPage() without a page component.

The helpers are in files/methods.py. The REST permission classes in cms/permissions.py call them. Views and serializers use the permission classes.

def is_mediacms_editor(user):
    """Whether user is MediaCMS editor"""

    editor = False
    try:
        if user.is_superuser or user.is_manager or user.is_editor:
            editor = True
    except BaseException:
        pass
    return editor

docs.title: files.methods.user_is_pending_approval(user)

True when this signed-in user may browse but may not change the library.

Source code in files/methods.py 
def user_is_pending_approval(user):
    """True when this signed-in user may browse but may not change the library."""
    if not getattr(settings, "USERS_NEEDS_TO_BE_APPROVED", False):
        return False
    if not getattr(user, "is_authenticated", False):
        return False
    if getattr(user, "is_superuser", False):
        return False
    return not getattr(user, "is_approved", False)

docs.title: user_allowed_to_upload
docs.text:
Takes the request. It checks these rules in this order:

  1. An anonymous user cannot upload.
  2. A pending user cannot upload.
  3. An editor, manager, or superuser can upload.
  4. A user who has reached NUMBER_OF_MEDIA_USER_CAN_UPLOAD cannot upload.
  5. The setting CAN_ADD_MEDIA decides: all, email_verified, or advancedUser.

docs.title: files.methods.user_allowed_to_upload(request)
docs.text:
Any custom logic for whether a user is allowed to upload content lives here

Source code in files/methods.py 
def user_allowed_to_upload(request):
    """Any custom logic for whether a user is allowed
    to upload content lives here
    """

    if request.user.is_anonymous:
        return False
    if user_is_pending_approval(request.user):
        return False
    if is_mediacms_editor(request.user):
        return True

    # Check if user has reached the maximum number of uploads
    if hasattr(settings, 'NUMBER_OF_MEDIA_USER_CAN_UPLOAD'):
        if models.Media.objects.filter(user=request.user).count() >= settings.NUMBER_OF_MEDIA_USER_CAN_UPLOAD:
            return False

    if settings.CAN_ADD_MEDIA == "all":
        return True
    elif settings.CAN_ADD_MEDIA == "email_verified":
        if request.user.email_is_verified:
            return True
    elif settings.CAN_ADD_MEDIA == "advancedUser":
        if request.user.advancedUser:
            return True
    return False

docs.title: can_edit_category
docs.text: A portal manager can always edit a category. When USE_RBAC is on and the category is an RBAC category, a manager of that category can also edit it. A contributor cannot rename a category.

docs.title: files.methods.can_edit_category(user, category)
docs.text:
Whether this user may change a category's title, description or thumbnail.

Portal managers always may, and beyond them only the managers of an RBAC category, which belongs to their group rather than the portal at large. A contributor may put media in such a category but not rename it.

Source code in files/methods.py 
def can_edit_category(user, category):
    """Whether this user may change a category's title, description or thumbnail.

    Portal managers always may, and beyond them only the managers of an RBAC category,
    which belongs to their group rather than the portal at large. A contributor may put
    media in such a category but not rename it.
    """
    if not (user and user.is_authenticated):
        return False

    if is_mediacms_manager(user):
        return True

    if getattr(settings, "USE_RBAC", False) and category.is_rbac_category:
        return user.has_manager_access_to_category(category)

    return False

docs.title: REST permission classes
docs.text:
The module cms.permissions holds the permission classes for the REST API. Each class is a Django REST Framework BasePermission.

Class Rule IsAuthorizedToAdd A write request needs user_allowed_to_upload. A read request is allowed. IsAuthorizedToAddComment A write request needs user_allowed_to_comment. A read request is allowed. IsUserOrManager A write request is allowed for the owner, a manager, or a superuser. IsUserOrEditor A write request is allowed for the owner, an editor, a manager, or a superuser. IsMediaContributorOrEditor A read of a private media item needs member access or editor rights. A PUT or PATCH is also allowed for an RBAC contributor of the media.

class IsUserOrManager(permissions.BasePermission):
    """To be used in cases where request.user is either the
    object owner, or anyone amongst MediaCMS managers
    or superusers
    """

    def has_object_permission(self, request, view, obj):
        if request.method in permissions.SAFE_METHODS:

        if request.user.is_superuser:
            return True

            return True

class IsMediaContributorOrEditor(permissions.BasePermission):
    def has_object_permission(self, request, view, obj):
        if request.method in permissions.SAFE_METHODS:
            if obj.state != "private":
                return True
            return request.user.is_authenticated and (request.user.has_member_access_to_media(obj) or is_mediacms_editor(request.user))
        if request.user.is_superuser or is_mediacms_editor(request.user):
            return True
        if obj.user == request.user:
            return True
        if request.method in ("PUT", "PATCH"):
            return request.user.has_contributor_access_to_media(obj)
        return False

def user_allowed_to_comment(request):
    """Any custom logic for whether a user is allowed
    to comment lives here
    """
    if request.user.is_anonymous:
        return False
    if request.user.is_superuser:
        return True

    # Default is "all"
    if not hasattr(settings, "CAN_COMMENT") or settings.CAN_COMMENT == "all":
        return True
    elif settings.CAN_COMMENT == "email_verified":
        if request.user.email_is_verified:
            return True
    elif settings.CAN_COMMENT == "advancedUser":
        if request.user.advancedUser:
            return True
    return False

docs.title: The listable rule
docs.text:
A media item appears in public listings only when its field listable is true. Media.save() in files/models/media.py sets listable on each save. The value is true when all of these are true:

Condition Meaning state == "public" The media is public. Private and unlisted media never appear in listings. encoding_status == "success" Encoding finished without error. is_reviewed is True An editor or manager reviewed the media. When MEDIA_IS_REVIEWED is True, new media starts as reviewed.

Otherwise listable is false. A listable media item is not the same as an accessible media item. A user can open an unlisted media item by its URL even though it is not listable.

docs.title: RBAC role names
docs.text:
The rbac app has three role names. They are in RBACRole in rbac/models.py. A role belongs to one user in one RBACGroup. Categories link to groups. The setting USE_RBAC turns the feature on.

Role name Value What it allows in the categories of the group Member member See the media in the categories. Contributor contributor See the media. Add media to the categories. Edit media. A contributor cannot rename a category. Manager manager Do what a contributor does. Edit the category title, description, and thumbnail.

Warning

The RBAC role manager is not the portal role manager. The portal role is the user flag is_manager. It applies to the whole portal. The RBAC role applies to the categories of one group. Use is_mediacms_manager for the portal role and user.has_manager_access_to_category(category) for the RBAC role.

See Permissions and RBAC for the operator view.

docs.title: Roles
docs.text:
A role is a set of powers. MediaCMS has six roles: anonymous, viewer, editor, manager, staff, and superuser. A signed-in user can also be in the pending state, which limits the user to reading.

Role Short description Page Anonymous A visitor who is not signed in. Browses listable media. Anonymous Pending A signed-in user who waits for approval. Reads only. Pending approval Viewer A signed-in user. Manages own media, comments, playlists, and shares. Viewer Editor A viewer who can also open Manage media and Manage comments and review media. Editor Manager An editor who can also manage users. Manager Staff A user who can open the admin portal. Staff Superuser A staff user with full access, content migration, and site upgrade. Superuser

The pending state applies to a signed-in user when the setting USERS_NEEDS_TO_BE_APPROVED is True. Pending is not a separate permission flag.

To see all roles side by side, open Compare roles.

docs.title: How roles work
docs.text:
Each role maps to flags on the user account.

Flag Meaning is_approved An approver accepted the account. Matters only when USERS_NEEDS_TO_BE_APPROVED is True. advancedUser The user can add media when CAN_ADD_MEDIA is advancedUser. is_editor The user is an editor. is_manager The user is a manager. is_staff The user can open the admin portal. is_superuser The user has every power.

A manager has all editor powers. A superuser has all manager and editor powers. A staff user does not get Manage pages unless the user is also an editor, a manager, or a superuser.

docs.title: MediaCMS Architecture
docs.text:
Django checks the user flags on every request. The checks happen in the views and in the REST API.

    signedIn -- "No" --> anonymousRole["Anonymous"]
    signedIn -- "Yes" --> approved{"Approved or approval off?"}
    approved -- "No" --> pendingRole["Pending"]
    approved -- "Yes" --> viewerRole["Viewer"]
    viewerRole --> editorRole["Editor: is_editor"]
    editorRole --> managerRole["Manager: is_manager"]
    viewerRole --> staffRole["Staff: is_staff"]
    staffRole --> superuserRole["Superuser: is_superuser"]
    managerRole --> superuserRole

docs.title: Anonymous
docs.text: An anonymous user is a visitor who is not signed in.

docs.title: What an anonymous user can do
docs.text:
• Browse listable media on the home page, in categories, and in search results.
  • Play public media.
  • Open an unlisted media item when the user has the URL.
  • Read comments on public media.

docs.title: What an anonymous user cannot do
docs.text:
• Upload media.
  • Write comments.
  • Create playlists.
  • Open private media.
  • Open Manage pages or the admin portal.

Each write action asks the visitor to sign in. Select Sign in to continue.

Note

If GLOBAL_LOGIN_REQUIRED is True, the portal asks every visitor to sign in first.

docs.text:
1. Open the portal address in a browser.
  2. Look at the media on the home page.
  3. Select a media item to play it.
  4. Enter a word in the search field. Press Enter.

See Browse and play and Search.

docs.text:

  • A superuser has all manager and editor powers.

docs.title: Editor
docs.text: An editor is a user with the flag is_editor. An editor has all viewer powers.

docs.title: What an editor can do
docs.text:
• Open Manage media and Manage comments.
  • Open and edit the media of other users, including private media.
  • Mark media as reviewed.
  • Change the state of media to public, private, or unlisted.
  • Delete comments.
  • Clear reports on media.

docs.title: What an editor cannot do
docs.text:
• Open Manage users. Only managers and superusers can open it.
  • Approve users.
  • Open the admin portal, unless the user is also staff.

docs.title: Review media
docs.text:
Review applies when MEDIA_IS_REVIEWED is False. Media is not listable until a reviewer marks it as reviewed.

  1. Open Manage media.
  2. Select the Needs review filter.
  3. Open a media item. Check the title, the description, and the file.
  4. Select the media item. Select Mark as reviewed.
  5. Check that the media shows in public listings. The state must be public and the encoding status must be success.

See Manage media and comments and Review and publish.

docs.title: Manager
docs.text: A manager is a user with the flag is_manager. A manager has all editor powers and can also manage users.

docs.title: What a manager can do
docs.text:
• Do everything an editor can do.
  • Open Manage users.
  • Approve and disapprove users when USERS_NEEDS_TO_BE_APPROVED is True.
  • Assign the editor role and the advancedUser flag to users.
  • Change the password of a user who is not a superuser.

docs.title: What a manager cannot do
docs.text:
• Open the admin portal at /admin/. A manager is not Django staff by default.
  • Change the password of a superuser.
  • Run a content migration or a site upgrade.

Note

An administrator can give the same user the staff flag. Then the user can open the admin portal as well.

docs.title: Pending approval
docs.text: A pending user is a signed-in user whose account is not approved yet.

docs.title: When a user is pending
docs.text:
A user is pending when all of these conditions are true:

  1. The setting USERS_NEEDS_TO_BE_APPROVED is True.
  2. The user is signed in.
  3. The field is_approved is False.
  4. The user is not a superuser.

Superusers skip the approval check.

docs.title: What a pending user can do
docs.text:
• Browse and play listable media.
  • Read comments.
  • Open the profile page.

docs.title: What a pending user cannot do
docs.text:
• Upload media.
  • Edit media.
  • Write comments or create playlists.
  • Open Manage pages.

The portal refuses these actions. The portal does not block sign-in.

docs.title: Leave the pending state
docs.text:
A manager or a superuser must approve the account. They can use one of these ways:

  1. Open Manage users. Use the approve action on the user.
  2. Open the user in the admin portal. Select Is approved.
  3. Edit the user profile. Select Is approved.

See Manage users.

docs.title: MediaCMS Architecture
docs.text:
The function user_is_pending_approval in files/methods.py decides if a user is pending. The upload, edit, and Manage views call it and refuse a pending user. The middleware ApprovalMiddleware lets pending users through.

    superuserCheck -- "Yes" --> normal
    superuserCheck -- "No" --> approvedCheck{"is_approved is True?"}
    approvedCheck -- "Yes" --> normal
    approvedCheck -- "No" --> pendingNode["Pending: read only"]

docs.title: Staff
docs.text: A staff user has the Django flag is_staff. A staff user can open the admin portal.

docs.title: What a staff user can do
docs.text:
• Open the admin portal at /admin/. It shows a dashboard and the data tables.
  • Work with the tools in the admin portal: moderation, library, processing, people, and integrations.
  • Read and cancel tasks through the API at /api/v1/tasks.
  • Do everything a viewer can do.

docs.title: What a staff user cannot do
docs.text:
• Open Manage media, Manage users, or Manage comments. These pages stay closed unless the user is also an editor, a manager, or a superuser.
  • Run a content migration or a site upgrade. Only superusers can do this.

Note

The admin portal limits each staff user to the model permissions that an administrator granted.

docs.title: Open the admin portal
docs.text:
1. Sign in as a staff user.
  2. Open /admin/ in the browser.
  3. Look at the dashboard cards.
  4. Select a card to open the related table.

See Admin portal map and Processing.
