docs.title: Superuser
docs.text: A superuser has the Django flag is_superuser. A superuser has all staff, manager, editor, and viewer powers. The first admin user is a superuser.

docs.title: What a superuser can do
docs.text:
• Do everything a staff user can do.
  • Open the Manage pages. A superuser counts as an editor and a manager.
  • Skip the approval check, even when USERS_NEEDS_TO_BE_APPROVED is True.
  • Change any user, including the password of another superuser.
  • Run a content migration to import media from another platform.
  • Run a site upgrade to move an existing install to a new MediaCMS version.

docs.title: Content migration
docs.text:
Content migration imports media from Kaltura, YouTube, or Panopto. Only superusers can start it.

See Content migration.

docs.title: Site upgrade
docs.text:
Site upgrade moves an existing MediaCMS install to a new MediaCMS version. Only superusers can run it.

See Site upgrade.

docs.title: Protect superuser accounts
docs.text:
1. Give the superuser flag to as few people as possible.
  2. Use a strong, unique password for each superuser.
  3. Do not share superuser accounts.

docs.title: Viewer
docs.text: A viewer is a signed-in user without editor, manager, staff, or superuser powers. If approval is on, the viewer is approved.

docs.title: What a viewer can do
docs.text:
• Upload media, when the setting CAN_ADD_MEDIA allows it.
  • Edit and delete own media.
  • Open own private and unlisted media.
  • Write comments, when the setting CAN_COMMENT allows it.
  • Create playlists.
  • Share media and copy embed code.
  • Add captions to own media.
  • Trim own video.

A viewer cannot open Manage pages or the admin portal. A viewer cannot review media.

docs.title: From upload to listable
docs.text:
1. The viewer uploads a file. MediaCMS sets the state from PORTAL_WORKFLOW.
  2. For a video, Celery encodes the file. The encoding status becomes success.
  3. If MEDIA_IS_REVIEWED is False, an editor marks the media as reviewed.
  4. The media becomes listable when the state is public, the encoding succeeded, and the media is reviewed.

A viewer sees own media in the profile even when it is not listable.

  2. Open your media. Select the edit option. See Edit your media.
  3. Write a comment. See Comments and mentions.
  4. Create a playlist. See Playlists.
  5. Share a media item. See Share and embed.

docs.title: Create a content migration draft for a source platform and test the connection
docs.text:
Related guides: Content migration, Superuser role

Warning

Content migration imports media from another platform. It is not a site upgrade. For a site upgrade, read Superuser upgrade inventory.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
1. Open the portal in a desktop browser at 1280 by 800.
  2. Sign in as a superuser.
  3. Back up the database and the media_files directory.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Open Migrations in the top right menu. The address is /migrations.
The Migrations list page. The list is empty. The button New migration is visible.
  1. Select New migration.
  2. Select the source Kaltura.
  3. Enter Service URL, Partner ID, App token ID, and App token value.
  4. Select Test connection.
The new Kaltura migration form. The connection fields are filled. The result of Test connection shows counts and the list of categories.
  1. Select at least one top-level category.
  2. Select Save draft.
The page of the saved migration. The status is pending. The App token value shows a mask, not the secret.

docs.text:
The portal saves the migration as a draft. Test connection reads counts and loads the choices. It imports nothing. The portal never shows the stored secret.

Nothing is imported until you select Save and start, or you start the draft later.

docs.title: Run the upgrade_site inventory command and confirm that the migrations fast-forward
docs.text:
Related guides: Site upgrade, Update, Superuser role

Warning

A site upgrade moves your own MediaCMS install to a new version. It is not a content migration. For media from Kaltura, YouTube, or Panopto, read Superuser content migration.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
1. Open a terminal window on the server. Make the window about 1280 by 800 pixels.
  2. Back up the source database with pg_dump.
  3. Copy the media_files directory.
  4. Start a one-off container of the new image in the application directory. Point its settings at the source database.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Run the command.
python manage.py upgrade_site inventory --previous /audit/previous
A terminal after the inventory command. One line of JSON shows the keys migrations, checks, and reports. The key fast_forward is true.
  1. Read the key migrations. Find fast_forward.
  2. Check that problems is an empty list.
  3. Read pending. It lists the migrations that the new image adds.
  4. Read checks and reports. Note each item for the upgrade.

docs.title: Expected result
docs.text:
The output is one line of JSON. fast_forward is true. problems is empty. The command does not change the source database.

Go to the next step only when fast_forward is true. The next step is upgrade_site scratch.

docs.title: If this fails
docs.text:
• If fast_forward is false and a problem has the reason missing, the database has a migration that the image does not have. Stop. Use an image that has the migration.
  • If a problem has the reason do-not-fake, the migration has the same name but different file content. Stop. Do not fake this migration. Ask for help.
  • If the output has no data about the old install, the old tree is not mounted. Check the path /audit/previous. A do-not-fake problem is found only when the old tree is mounted.
  • The command reads data only. After the upgrade, open Site > Health. See Superuser health.
